Enumeration for different colormap types. 

Enumeration of colormap types for image processing.

This enumeration is defined in the highmap/colormap.\+hpp file and is used for selecting the colormap to be applied during colorization.

This enumeration defines various colormap options that can be used for visualizing data in image processing. Each colormap provides a different color mapping scheme, which can be applied to grayscale images or data to enhance visual interpretation. \begin{DoxyEnumFields}{Enumerator}

Converts an Open\+CV {\ttfamily cv\+::\+Mat} to a 2D {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} with optional value scaling to \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. 

This function converts an Open\+CV {\ttfamily cv\+::\+Mat} object into a 2D {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}}. The conversion process creates a new {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} object and copies the data from the {\ttfamily cv\+::\+Mat} into this {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}}. If the {\ttfamily remap\+\_\+values} parameter is set to {\ttfamily true} (the default), the values in the resulting {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} will be scaled to the interval \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If set to {\ttfamily false}, the values will be copied directly without scaling. Modifications to the {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} will not affect the original {\ttfamily cv\+::\+Mat} and vice versa.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em mat} & Reference to the Open\+CV {\ttfamily cv\+::\+Mat} object that will be converted. \\
\hline
{\em remap\+\_\+values} & A boolean flag indicating whether to scale the values to \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If {\ttfamily true}, the values will be scaled; if {\ttfamily false}, they will be copied directly. Default is {\ttfamily true}. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A 2D {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} object containing a copy of the data from the input {\ttfamily cv\+::\+Mat}, with optional scaling to the interval \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Point-\/wise alteration\+: locally enforce a new elevation value while maintaining the \textquotesingle{}shape\textquotesingle{} of the heightmap. 

This function modifies the elevation values in the input array based on a cloud of points that specify the coordinates and variations for the alterations. The function ensures that the shape of the heightmap is preserved while applying these local changes.

The alteration is performed using a kernel with a minimal radius ({\ttfamily ir}) and the intensity of the alterations is scaled based on the {\ttfamily footprint\+\_\+ratio}. The {\ttfamily shift} parameter allows for introducing noise or offset in the alteration process, and the {\ttfamily scale} parameter is used to adjust the domain of the alteration.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be altered. The elevation values in this array will be adjusted according to the cloud data. \\
\hline
{\em cloud} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud} object that defines the coordinates and elevation variations for the alterations. This object provides the necessary data for applying the local changes. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Alteration kernel minimal radius. This parameter defines the minimum size of the kernel used for local alterations. \\
\hline
{\em footprint\+\_\+ratio} & Defines how the radius of the alteration scales with the variation intensity. A higher ratio results in a larger footprint of the alterations. \\
\hline
{\em shift} & Noise shift specified as a vector \{xs, ys\} for each direction, relative to a unit domain. This allows for adding random offsets to the alteration process. \\
\hline
{\em scale} & Domain scaling in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. This parameter adjusts the domain size over which the alteration is applied.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Generate a heightmap from a coarse grid of control points with defined elevation values. 

This function creates a heightmap by interpolating elevation values provided at specific control points on a coarse grid. The result is a finer resolution heightmap where the elevation values are smoothly distributed over the entire grid.

The interpolation is performed using a Gaussian function, with the {\ttfamily width\+\_\+factor} parameter controlling the half-\/width of the base Gaussian function used for smoothing. Optionally, noise can be added using the provided {\ttfamily p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} and {\ttfamily p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} arrays, and the heightmap can be adjusted by a local wavenumber multiplier specified by {\ttfamily p\+\_\+stretching}. The {\ttfamily bbox} parameter defines the domain bounding box for the heightmap.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Dimensions of the output array (heightmap). \\
\hline
{\em values} & Elevation values at the control points specified on a coarse grid. This 2D vector holds the elevation data at each control point. \\
\hline
{\em width\+\_\+factor} & Factor applied to the half-\/width of the Gaussian function used for smoothing the elevations. A value of 1.\+0 represents the default smoothing width. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Optional pointer to an input noise array affecting the x-\/direction. If provided, it is used to add noise to the elevation values. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Optional pointer to an input noise array affecting the y-\/direction. If provided, it is used to add noise to the elevation values. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+stretching} & Optional pointer to an input array that acts as a local wavenumber multiplier. If provided, it adjusts the elevation values according to the local wavenumber. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Domain bounding box specified as a vector \{xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax\}. This defines the extent of the heightmap in the coordinate space. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} A new array representing the generated heightmap with interpolated elevation values.
\end{DoxyReturn}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::reverse\+\_\+midpoint (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{float}]{noise\+\_\+scale = {\ttfamily 1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{float}]{threshold = {\ttfamily 0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Apply the reverse midpoint displacement algorithm to the input array. 

This function implements the reverse midpoint displacement algorithm as described in Belhadj et al. (2005). The algorithm generates a terrain-\/like structure by applying displacement to the values in the input array based on random noise. The function can be tuned using the {\ttfamily seed} parameter for random number generation, {\ttfamily noise\+\_\+scale} for controlling the amplitude of the noise, and {\ttfamily threshold} for setting a background value.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array to which the reverse midpoint displacement algorithm will be applied. The array\textquotesingle{}s values are modified to produce the output terrain. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed number used to initialize the random number generator for reproducibility. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+scale} & Amplitude of the noise applied during the displacement process. A higher value results in more pronounced terrain features. \\
\hline
{\em threshold} & Threshold \textquotesingle{}background\textquotesingle{} value used to influence the displacement algorithm. Values below this threshold may be treated differently depending on the algorithm\textquotesingle{}s design. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} The output array after applying the reverse midpoint displacement algorithm. This array contains the modified values representing the generated terrain.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Generate a heightmap based on a set of ridgelines and a specified slope. 

This function creates a heightmap using a set of ridgelines defined by their x, y, and z coordinates, and applies a specified slope to the ridgelines. The function can optionally apply smoothing, adjust the ridge edge width, and clamp values below a minimum threshold. Additional noise and stretching parameters can be applied to modify the resulting heightmap.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & The dimensions of the output array (heightmap). \\
\hline
{\em xr} & A vector of x-\/coordinates defining ridge segments. \\
\hline
{\em yr} & A vector of y-\/coordinates defining ridge segments. \\
\hline
{\em zr} & A vector of z-\/coordinates defining ridge segments. \\
\hline
{\em slope} & The slope applied to the ridgelines. Can be negative to invert the slope. \\
\hline
{\em k\+\_\+smoothing} & Smoothing parameter to control the smoothness of the ridgelines. \\
\hline
{\em width} & Width of the ridge edges. Determines how broad the ridges appear. \\
\hline
{\em vmin} & Minimum value for the heightmap. Values below this threshold will be clamped to {\ttfamily vmin}. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box for the entire domain, defining the area covered by the heightmap. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Pointer to an optional array for x-\/direction noise to apply to the heightmap. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Pointer to an optional array for y-\/direction noise to apply to the heightmap. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+stretching} & Pointer to an optional array for local wavenumber multipliers to stretch the ridges. \\
\hline
{\em bbox\+\_\+array} & Bounding box for the array domain, defining the spatial extent of the heightmap.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Generate a heightmap based on a set of ridgelines with quadratic Bezier interpolation. 

This function creates a heightmap using ridgelines defined by their x, y, and z coordinates. The ridgelines are interpolated using quadratic Bezier curves to smooth the transitions. The function applies a specified slope to the ridgelines and can optionally apply smoothing, adjust ridge edge width, and clamp values below a minimum threshold. Additional noise and stretching parameters can be used to modify the resulting heightmap.

\hline
{\em zr} & A vector of z-\/coordinates defining ridge segments, organized in groups of three (control points of the Bezier curves). \\
\hline
{\em slope} & The slope applied to the ridgelines. Can be negative to invert the slope. \\
\hline

\hline

\hline

\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box for the entire domain, defining the area covered by the heightmap. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Pointer to an optional array for x-\/direction noise to apply to the heightmap. \\

{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Pointer to an optional array for y-\/direction noise to apply to the heightmap. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+stretching} & Pointer to an optional array for local wavenumber multipliers to stretch the ridges. \\
\hline
{\em bbox\+\_\+array} & Bounding box for the array domain, defining the spatial extent of the heightmap.\\
\hline

Generate a heightmap by stamping a kernel at predefined locations. 

This function creates a heightmap by stamping a specified kernel at given x, y, and z coordinates. The kernel can be scaled and manipulated based on the z-\/coordinates of the stamping points, and can be optionally flipped or rotated. The heightmap is generated by blending the results using the specified blending method. Randomization options are available for kernel manipulation.

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::elevation\+\_\+from\+\_\+sparse\+\_\+constraints (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{mountains,  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+coastline = {\ttfamily nullptr},  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+boundary = {\ttfamily nullptr},  }\item[{float}]{mountain\+\_\+elevation = {\ttfamily 1.0f},  }\item[{float}]{coastline\+\_\+elevation = {\ttfamily 0.0f},  }\item[{float}]{boundary\+\_\+elevation = {\ttfamily -\/1.0f},  }\item[{int}]{iterations\+\_\+max = {\ttfamily 500},  }\item[{float}]{tolerance = {\ttfamily 1e-\/5\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+noise = {\ttfamily nullptr},  }\item[{float}]{noise\+\_\+amplitude = {\ttfamily 0.0f} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Synthesize a smooth heightmap from sparse elevation constraints using GPU harmonic interpolation (Laplacian PDE). 

This function allows generating a continuous terrain elevation model from sparse sketch data by treating the provided constraints as Dirichlet boundary conditions and solving the discrete Laplace equation (\$\textbackslash{}\+Delta z = 0\$) using GPU-\/accelerated Red-\/\+Black SOR.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em mountains} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} specifying mountain peak/ridge elevations (\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 0). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+coastline} & Optional pointer to coastline mask (fixed to coastline\+\_\+elevation). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+boundary} & Optional pointer to outer boundary/ocean mask (fixed to boundary\+\_\+elevation). If null, a 1-\/pixel boundary border around the domain perimeter is used. \\
\hline
{\em mountain\+\_\+elevation} & Target elevation scaling for mountains (default\+: 1.\+0). \\
\hline
{\em coastline\+\_\+elevation} & Elevation at coastline (default\+: 0.\+0). \\
\hline
{\em boundary\+\_\+elevation} & Elevation at boundary/ocean (default\+: -\/1.\+0). \\
\hline
{\em iterations\+\_\+max} & Max iterations for GPU solver (default\+: 500). \\
\hline
{\em tolerance} & Convergence tolerance for early exit (default\+: 1e-\/5). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise} & Optional noise array to modulate the free terrain regions. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+amplitude} & Amplitude of optional noise detail (default\+: 0.\+0). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} The resulting smooth synthesized heightmap.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Return the \textquotesingle{}exclusion\textquotesingle{} blending of two arrays. 

The exclusion blend mode creates a blend that is similar to the difference blend mode but with lower contrast. It produces an effect that is often used in image editing for special effects. For more details, see \href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blend_modes}{\texttt{ https\+://en.\+wikipedia.\+org/wiki/\+Blend\+\_\+modes}}.

\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} values are expected to be in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}.
\end{DoxyWarning}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::blend\+\_\+power\+\_\+law (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const std\+::vector$<$ const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} $>$ \&}]{arrays,  }\item[{float}]{alpha = {\ttfamily 0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Return the power law blending of a set of arrays. 

Blends two (or more) arrays using power law averaging\+:  \[
f_\text{blend} = \frac{\sum_i f_i^{\alpha+1}}{\sum_i f_i^\alpha}
\] The behavior varies with the bias $\alpha$ from a simple average of the heights at each node when $\alpha=0$, approaching $\max(f_i)$ as $\alpha \to \infty$.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em arrays} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} references to blend. \\
\hline
{\em alpha} & Power law exponent (default\+: 0.\+0). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Resulting array after power law blending.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Transfers spatial details from a source array onto a target array. 

This function applies a high-\/pass spatial filter to the {\ttfamily source} array (using a smoothing pulse of radius {\ttfamily ir}) to extract its high-\/frequency content. That content is then scaled by {\ttfamily amplitude} and blended with the {\ttfamily target} array. Optionally, the target can be prefiltered before blending.

The result is a new array that combines the base structure of {\ttfamily target} with the high-\/frequency details from {\ttfamily source}.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em source} & The input array providing high-\/frequency details. \\
\hline
{\em target} & The input array providing the base structure. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius (in pixels or samples) for the smoothing filter used to separate low/high frequencies. \\
\hline
{\em amplitude} & Scaling factor applied to the high-\/frequency content extracted from {\ttfamily source}. \\
\hline
{\em target\+\_\+prefiltering} & If true, {\ttfamily target} is smoothed before blending to better integrate with the transferred details.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} containing the target data enhanced by the source\textquotesingle{}s high-\/frequency information.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Performs linear extrapolation of values at the borders of an array (e.\+g., {\ttfamily i = 0}, {\ttfamily j = 0}, etc.) based on the inner values of the array. 

This function modifies the borders of the input array by applying a linear extrapolation method, which uses the values inside the array to estimate and fill in the border values. The extrapolation is influenced by a relaxation coefficient ({\ttfamily sigma}) and a buffer depth ({\ttfamily nbuffer}), which determines how many layers of the border are extrapolated.

\hline

\hline
{\em sigma} & Optional relaxation coefficient that adjusts the influence of inner values on the extrapolated border values. Default is 0.\+0.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Applies a falloff effect to the input array based on distance. 

This function modifies the elements of the input {\ttfamily array} by applying a falloff effect, which decreases the values based on their distance from a central point or area. The strength of the falloff, the type of distance function used, and optional noise can be specified.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Reference to the array that will be modified by the falloff effect. \\
\hline

\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise} & Optional pointer to an array that provides noise to be added to the falloff effect. If nullptr (default), no noise is added. \\
\hline

\hline

Creates a periodic array in both directions using a stitching operation that minimizes errors at the boundaries. 

This function generates a new array that is periodic in both directions by applying a stitching operation at the boundaries. The stitching process aims to minimize discrepancies, creating a seamless transition between the edges of the array. The {\ttfamily overlap} parameter determines the extent of the overlap during the stitching, based on the half-\/size of the domain. If {\ttfamily overlap} is set to 1, the transition spans the entire domain.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Reference to the input array to be made periodic. \\
\hline
{\em overlap} & A float value representing the overlap based on the domain\textquotesingle{}s half-\/size. An overlap of 1 means the transition spans the whole domain. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} A new array that is periodic in both directions with minimized boundary errors.
\end{DoxyReturn}

The {\ttfamily tiling} parameter specifies the number of tiles in the horizontal and vertical directions.

Picks a boundary cell using weighted random selection. 

Selects a cell on the specified boundary, where each candidate is assigned a weight. Higher weights increase the probability of selection.

Optional weighting factors\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item favor\+\_\+boundary\+\_\+center\+: favors cells near the boundary center.
\item favor\+\_\+lower\+\_\+elevation\+: favors lower values in {\ttfamily z} (normalized).
\item favor\+\_\+sinks\+: favors local minima (cells \texorpdfstring{$<$}{<}= neighbors).
\end{DoxyItemize}

Weights are combined multiplicatively. Selection is deterministic given {\ttfamily seed}.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input 2D scalar field. \\
\hline
{\em boundary} & Boundary to sample from. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed. \\
\hline
{\em favor\+\_\+boundary\+\_\+center} & Enable center bias. \\
\hline
{\em favor\+\_\+lower\+\_\+elevation} & Enable low-\/value bias. \\
\hline
{\em favor\+\_\+sinks} & Enable sink bias.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Selected boundary cell coordinates.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Dig a path on a heightmap. 

This function modifies a heightmap array by "{}digging"{} a path into it based on the provided path. The path is represented by a {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Path}{Path}} object, and the function adjusts the height values in the {\ttfamily z} array to create the appearance of a dug path. The width, border decay, and flattening radius parameters control the characteristics of the dig. Optionally, the path can be forced to have a monotonically decreasing elevation.

Modifies the elevation array to carve a river along a specified path. 

This function adjusts the elevation values in the input array {\ttfamily z} to simulate a river along the provided {\ttfamily path}. It incorporates parameters for riverbed and riverbank slopes, noise effects, and merging behavior to create a realistic river profile.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & The input 2D array representing the elevation map. This array will be modified in place. \\
\hline
{\em path} & The path along which the river is to be carved, represented as a sequence of points, with coordinates with respect to a unit-\/square. \\
\hline
{\em riverbank\+\_\+talus} & The slope of the riverbank, controlling how steep the river\textquotesingle{}s edges are. \\
\hline
{\em merging\+\_\+ir} & The merging radius, specifying how far the effects of multiple rivers combine. \\
\hline
{\em riverbed\+\_\+talus} & The slope of the riverbed, controlling how steep the riverbed is (default\+: 0.\+0). \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+ratio} & The proportion of random noise applied to the river\textquotesingle{}s shape for realism (default\+: 0.\+9). \\
\hline
{\em seed} & The seed for the random noise generator, ensuring reproducibility (default\+: 0).\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Blends a flatbed carve into an existing heightmap. 

Carves and blends a flatbed shape along a path into the provided array, using a smooth falloff mask.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Heightmap to modify in place. \\

\hline
{\em vmin} & Base height value. \\
\hline
{\em depth} & Bed depth. \\
\hline
{\em falloff\+\_\+distance} & Falloff width outside the bed. \\
\hline
{\em outer\+\_\+slope} & Linear slope beyond the bed. \\
\hline
{\em preserve\+\_\+bedshape} & Preserve relative bed shape under radial noise. \\
\hline
{\em radial\+\_\+profile} & Radial profile type. \\
\hline
{\em radial\+\_\+profile\+\_\+parameter} & Shape parameter for the profile. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+falloff\+\_\+mask} & Optional output falloff mask. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+r} & Optional radial noise. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & World-\/space bounding box.\\
\hline

Carves a trench along a given path into a heightmap. 

This function modifies the input heightmap by carving a trench defined by a polyline path. The trench shape is controlled both longitudinally (along the path) and radially (across the path). Optional noise and scaling can be applied to introduce variations in width and depth.


\begin{DoxyParams}[1]{Parameters}
\mbox{\texttt{ in,out}}  & {\em z} & Heightmap to modify (2D array of elevations). \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em path} & Polyline defining the trench centerline. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em width} & Base width of the trench. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em enable\+\_\+width\+\_\+depth\+\_\+scaling} & If true, modulates trench width based on local elevation difference. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em radial\+\_\+profile} & Type of radial profile used to shape the trench cross-\/section. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em radial\+\_\+profile\+\_\+parameter} & Parameter controlling the radial profile shape. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em longitudinal\+\_\+profile} & Controls how elevation evolves along the path (e.\+g., flat, increasing, decreasing). \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em elevation\+\_\+shift} & Global elevation offset applied along the path. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em shift\+\_\+ramp\+\_\+start\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of the path length used to smoothly ramp the elevation shift at the beginning. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em shift\+\_\+ramp\+\_\+end\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of the path length used to smoothly ramp the elevation shift at the end. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em min\+\_\+slope} & Minimum slope enforced between consecutive path points when monotonicity is required. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em k\+\_\+neighbors} & Number of nearest neighbors used for interpolation. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+r} & Optional pointer to a noise array used to locally perturb trench width (can be nullptr). \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ out}}  & {\em p\+\_\+bending\+\_\+mask} & Optional output mask representing blending weights (can be nullptr). \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em bbox} & Bounding box of the domain as (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax).\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}
The function assumes that {\ttfamily elevation\+\_\+shift} is non-\/zero when width-\/depth scaling is enabled, to avoid division by zero.
\end{DoxyWarning}

Colorize two scalar fields into a \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Texture}{Texture} using two custom colormaps and a color mixing method.

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Texture}{Texture}} hmap\+::colorize\+\_\+slope\+\_\+height\+\_\+heatmap (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{int}]{cmap }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Colorizes a slope height heatmap based on the gradient norms of a given array. 

This function computes a colorized heatmap using a two-\/dimensional histogram that considers the gradient norm of the input array. It normalizes both the input array values and their corresponding gradient norms, calculates a 2D histogram, and then applies a colormap to visualize the heatmap.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The input array for which the slope height heatmap is computed. This should be a 2D array representing height values. \\
\hline
{\em cmap} & An integer representing the colormap to be used for colorization. Colormap options depend on the colorization function used internally.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Texture}{Texture} representing the colorized heatmap, which visualizes the distribution of height values and their corresponding gradient norms.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The function normalizes the height values and gradient norms independently using the minimum and maximum values.
\item A 2D histogram is constructed, where each bin corresponds to a pair of normalized height and gradient values.
\item The colormap is then applied to this histogram to produce a colorized output.
\end{DoxyItemize}

\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
If the input array has a constant value (i.\+e., min == max), no normalization is applied, and the function may not produce meaningful results.
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}
Ensure that the input array is non-\/empty and has valid dimensions.
\end{DoxyWarning}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{coastal\_erosion\_diffusion()}{coastal\_erosion\_diffusion()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::coastal\+\_\+erosion\+\_\+diffusion (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{z,  }\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{water\+\_\+depth,  }\item[{float}]{additional\+\_\+depth,  }\item[{int}]{iterations = {\ttfamily 10},  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+mask = {\ttfamily nullptr},  }\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+water\+\_\+mask = {\ttfamily nullptr} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Simulates terrain diffusion due to coastal erosion. 

This function applies an iterative coastal erosion diffusion process on a terrain elevation array ({\ttfamily z}), taking into account the presence and depth of water. The erosion model smooths the terrain near shorelines while maintaining constant water-\/surface height.

At each iteration\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item A local water mask is computed using {\ttfamily water\+\_\+mask(water\+\_\+depth, z, additional\+\_\+depth)}.
\item The terrain elevations are smoothed (diffused) using a masked Laplacian filter, applied only near the water boundary.
\item The water depth is adjusted to preserve the total water surface height (i.\+e., {\ttfamily z + water\+\_\+depth} remains constant).
\end{DoxyItemize}

This results in a realistic simulation of coastal erosion processes where the terrain near the waterline is progressively smoothed and redistributed.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Reference to the terrain elevation array (modified in place). \\
\hline
{\em water\+\_\+depth} & Reference to the array representing water depth values (modified to preserve water surface level). \\
\hline
{\em additional\+\_\+depth} & Additional virtual water depth used to estimate the influence region of the shoreline during mask computation. \\
\hline
{\em iterations} & Number of erosion–diffusion iterations to apply. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+water\+\_\+mask} & Optional output pointer. If non-\/null, it receives the last computed water mask used during the final iteration.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::coastal\+\_\+erosion\+\_\+profile (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{z,  }\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{water\+\_\+depth,  }\item[{float}]{shore\+\_\+ground\+\_\+extent,  }\item[{float}]{shore\+\_\+water\+\_\+extent,  }\item[{float}]{slope\+\_\+shore = {\ttfamily 0.5\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{float}]{slope\+\_\+shore\+\_\+water = {\ttfamily 0.5\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{float}]{scarp\+\_\+extent\+\_\+ratio = {\ttfamily 0.5\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{bool}]{apply\+\_\+post\+\_\+filter = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{int}]{post\+\_\+filter\+\_\+iterations = {\ttfamily 3},  }\item[{bool}]{solid\+\_\+shore\+\_\+mask = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{float}]{scarp\+\_\+mask\+\_\+transition\+\_\+ratio = {\ttfamily 0.2\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+noise = {\ttfamily nullptr},  }\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+shore\+\_\+mask = {\ttfamily nullptr},  }\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+scarp\+\_\+mask = {\ttfamily nullptr} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Applies a coastal erosion profile to a terrain elevation field. 

This function modifies the elevation array {\ttfamily z} by carving a coastal profile at the interface between ground and water. It uses distance transforms both from ground regions and from water regions to determine how far each point is from the shoreline. According to this distance, the function applies\+:


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item A ground-\/side shore slope with an optional scarp transition.
\item A water-\/side underwater slope ensuring continuity with the ground slope.
\item An optional post-\/filtering step (Laplace smoothing) restricted to the shoreline region.
\end{DoxyItemize}

Water depth is adjusted after filtering to preserve the original water surface height.

Optionally, a shoreline mask can be returned describing the region influenced by the coastal transformation.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} of terrain elevations. Modified in-\/place. \\
\hline
{\em water\+\_\+depth} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} of water depths. Modified to preserve water surface height after terrain changes. \\
\hline
{\em shore\+\_\+ground\+\_\+extent} & Horizontal extent (in grid units) over which the ground-\/side shore profile is applied. \\
\hline
{\em shore\+\_\+water\+\_\+extent} & Horizontal extent (in grid units) over which the underwater profile is applied. \\
\hline
{\em slope\+\_\+shore} & Ground-\/side slope magnitude of the coastal profile. Expressed in elevation units per domain width. \\
\hline
{\em slope\+\_\+shore\+\_\+water} & Water-\/side slope magnitude of the underwater profile. Expressed similarly to {\ttfamily slope\+\_\+shore}. \\
\hline
{\em scarp\+\_\+extent\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio defining the relative extent of the scarp region. A value in \mbox{[}0,1\mbox{]}\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item 0 → no scarp, only slope
\item 1 → all scarp 
\end{DoxyItemize}\\
\hline
{\em apply\+\_\+post\+\_\+filter} & If true, applies Laplacian smoothing to {\ttfamily z} restricted to shoreline areas. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+shore\+\_\+mask} & Optional output pointer. If non-\/null, receives the shoreline mask (values in \mbox{[}0,1\mbox{]}) indicating where the coastal transformation was applied.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Fill the depressions of the heightmap using the Planchon-\/\+Darboux algorithm. 

Fill heightmap depressions to ensure that every cell can be connected to the boundaries following a downward slope {\bfseries [Planchon2002]}.

Generates a modified bedrock heightmap from an input elevation array. 

This function adjusts elevations based on overall height and local slope\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Reduces values relative to the elevation range using {\ttfamily elevation\+\_\+strength}.
\item Reduces values in steep areas using {\ttfamily slope\+\_\+strength} and {\ttfamily slope\+\_\+limit}.
\end{DoxyItemize}


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input elevation array. \\
\hline
{\em elevation\+\_\+strength} & Strength of elevation-\/based adjustment. \\
\hline
{\em slope\+\_\+strength} & Strength of slope-\/based adjustment. \\
\hline
{\em slope\+\_\+limit} & Slope threshold for slope-\/based adjustment. \\
\hline
{\em zmin} & Minimum elevation to consider (computed from z if zmin \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} zmax). \\
\hline
{\em zmax} & Maximum elevation to consider (computed from z if zmin \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} zmax). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Modified bedrock heightmap.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Perform hydraulic erosion on a triangulated terrain mesh. 

Iteratively updates elevations using a drainage model with uplift, slope constraints, and spatially varying erodibility.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em mesh} & Input/output terrain mesh. \\
\hline
{\em erodibility} & Per-\/vertex erodibility coefficients. \\
\hline
{\em max\+\_\+slope} & Per-\/vertex maximum slope constraint. \\
\hline
{\em m\+\_\+exp} & Exponent controlling flow response. \\
\hline
{\em uplift\+\_\+rate} & Constant uplift applied each iteration. \\
\hline
{\em tolerance} & Convergence threshold on elevation updates. \\
\hline
{\em max\+\_\+iterations} & Maximum number of erosion iterations.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply hydraulic erosion to a heightmap using an adaptive mesh. 

Converts the input heightmap to a triangulated mesh, performs erosion, and interpolates the result back to a grid.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input heightmap. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed for point sampling. \\
\hline
{\em control\+\_\+points\+\_\+count} & Number of mesh control points. \\
\hline
{\em m\+\_\+exp} & Flow response exponent. \\
\hline
{\em uplift\+\_\+rate} & Constant uplift per iteration. \\
\hline
{\em tolerance} & Convergence threshold. \\
\hline
{\em max\+\_\+iterations} & Maximum number of iterations. \\
\hline
{\em smin} & Minimum slope constraint. \\
\hline
{\em smax} & Maximum slope constraint. \\
\hline
{\em strength} & Blending factor between original and eroded terrain. \\
\hline
{\em scale\+\_\+erodibility\+\_\+with\+\_\+z} & Modulate erodibility with elevation. \\
\hline
{\em erodibility\+\_\+distrib\+\_\+exp} & Exponent for erodibility distribution. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Optional X displacement field. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Optional Y displacement field.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Eroded heightmap.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Apply hydraulic erosion based on a flow accumulation map, alternative formulation. 


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input array representing the terrain elevation. \\
\hline
{\em c\+\_\+erosion} & Erosion coefficient controlling the intensity of erosion. \\
\hline
{\em talus\+\_\+ref} & Reference talus used to locally define the flow-\/partition exponent. Small values lead to thinner flow streams (see {\ttfamily \doxylink{namespacehmap_a58ba4910af868f70849f343e0c73adf3}{flow\+\_\+accumulation\+\_\+dinf}}). \\
\hline
{\em deposition\+\_\+ir} & Kernel radius for sediment deposition. If greater than 1, a smoothing effect is applied. \\
\hline
{\em deposition\+\_\+scale\+\_\+ratio} & Scaling factor for sediment deposition. \\
\hline
{\em gradient\+\_\+power} & Exponent applied to the terrain gradient to control erosion intensity. \\
\hline
{\em gradient\+\_\+scaling\+\_\+ratio} & Scaling factor for gradient-\/based erosion. \\
\hline
{\em gradient\+\_\+prefilter\+\_\+ir} & Kernel radius for pre-\/filtering the terrain gradient. \\
\hline
{\em saturation\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio controlling the water saturation threshold for erosion processes. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+bedrock} & Pointer to an optional lower elevation limit. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+moisture\+\_\+map} & Pointer to the moisture map (rainfall quantity), expected to be in \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+erosion\+\_\+map\mbox{[}out\mbox{]}} & Pointer to the erosion map, provided as an output field. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+flow\+\_\+map\mbox{[}out\mbox{]}} & Pointer to the flow accumulation map, provided as an output field. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Kernel radius. If {\ttfamily ir \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 1}, a cone kernel is used to carve channel flow erosion.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::hydraulic\+\_\+stream\+\_\+upscale\+\_\+amplification (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{z,  }\item[{float}]{c\+\_\+erosion,  }\item[{float}]{talus\+\_\+ref,  }\item[{int}]{upscaling\+\_\+levels = {\ttfamily 1},  }\item[{float}]{persistence = {\ttfamily 1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{int}]{ir = {\ttfamily 1},  }\item[{float}]{clipping\+\_\+ratio = {\ttfamily 10.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Applies hydraulic erosion with upscaling amplification. 

This function progressively upscales the input array {\ttfamily z} by powers of 2 and applies hydraulic erosion based on flow accumulation at each level of upscaling. After all upscaling levels are processed, the array is resampled back to its original resolution using bilinear interpolation.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input array representing elevation data. \\
\hline
{\em c\+\_\+erosion} & Erosion coefficient. \\
\hline
{\em talus\+\_\+ref} & Reference talus used to locally define the flow-\/partition exponent. Smaller values lead to thinner flow streams. \\
\hline
{\em upscaling\+\_\+levels} & Number of upscaling levels to apply. The function will resample the array at each level. \\
\hline
{\em persistence} & A scaling factor applied at each level to adjust the impact of the unary operation. Higher persistence values will amplify the effects at each level. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Kernel radius. If {\ttfamily ir \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 1}, a cone kernel is used to carve channel flow erosion. \\
\hline
{\em clipping\+\_\+ratio} & Flow accumulation clipping ratio.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The function first applies upscaling using bicubic resampling, performs hydraulic erosion at each level, and finally resamples the array back to its initial resolution using bilinear interpolation.
\end{DoxyNote}

Applies hydraulic erosion with upscaling amplification, with a post-\/processing intensity mask. 

Similar to the overloaded version, this function progressively upscales the input array {\ttfamily z} and applies hydraulic erosion. Additionally, an intensity mask {\ttfamily p\+\_\+mask} is applied as a post-\/processing step.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input array representing elevation data. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Intensity mask, expected in \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}, which is applied as a post-\/processing step. \\
\hline
{\em c\+\_\+erosion} & Erosion coefficient. \\
\hline
{\em talus\+\_\+ref} & Reference talus used to locally define the flow-\/partition exponent. Smaller values lead to thinner flow streams. \\
\hline
{\em upscaling\+\_\+levels} & Number of upscaling levels to apply. The function will resample the array at each level. \\
\hline
{\em persistence} & A scaling factor applied at each level to adjust the impact of the unary operation. Higher persistence values will amplify the effects at each level. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Kernel radius. If {\ttfamily ir \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 1}, a cone kernel is used to carve channel flow erosion. \\
\hline
{\em clipping\+\_\+ratio} & Flow accumulation clipping ratio.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
This version of the function applies an additional intensity mask as part of the upscaling amplification process.
\end{DoxyNote}

Exports a heightmap to various 3D file formats. 

This function exports the input heightmap array as a 3D asset in the specified format. The export can include different mesh types, elevation scaling, and optional texture and normal maps. The function supports optimized Delaunay triangulation for mesh generation, with a configurable maximum error.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em fname} & The name of the file to which the 3D asset will be exported. \\
\hline
{\em array} & The input heightmap array to be converted into a 3D asset. \\
\hline
{\em mesh\+\_\+type} & The type of mesh to generate (see {\ttfamily \doxylink{namespacehmap_ac81a92060b89699c4eb9826495d87250}{Mesh\+Type}}). \\
\hline
{\em export\+\_\+format} & The format in which to export the asset (see {\ttfamily \doxylink{namespacehmap_ac3d35efc6e5b596f508e2b17a5aa871b}{Asset\+Export\+Format}}). \\
\hline
{\em elevation\+\_\+scaling} & A scaling factor applied to the elevation values of the heightmap. Default is 0.\+2f. \\
\hline
{\em texture\+\_\+fname} & The name of the texture file to be applied to the asset (optional). \\
\hline
{\em normal\+\_\+map\+\_\+fname} & The name of the normal map file to be applied to the asset (optional). \\
\hline
{\em max\+\_\+error} & The maximum allowable error for optimized Delaunay triangulation. Default is 5e-\/4f. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
{\ttfamily true} if the export is successful, {\ttfamily false} otherwise. 
\end{DoxyReturn}

Export a 2D array as an ASCII-\/art string representation. 

This function rescales the input array to a given export resolution, remaps its values to the \mbox{[}0,1\mbox{]} range, and then converts each value to a character from a user-\/provided character map. The characters are arranged row by row to form a textual representation of the array, similar to rendering a heightmap in ASCII.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The input 2D array to be exported. \\
\hline
{\em export\+\_\+shape} & The desired shape (width, height) of the ASCII output. \\
\hline
{\em chars\+\_\+map} & A string containing characters ordered from "{}low"{} to "{}high"{} intensity. For example\+: "{} .\+:-\/=+\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}\#\%@"{}\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A string containing the ASCII-\/art representation of the array.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The function resamples the array using nearest-\/neighbor interpolation. 

The y-\/axis is flipped so that higher indices appear lower in the text output. 
\end{DoxyNote}

Exports a 2D array as a cubemap texture with continuity enforcement and overlapping regions. 

This function generates a cubemap texture from the input array {\ttfamily z}, resamples the data to fit the cubemap resolution with optional overlapping regions, and ensures seamless transitions between the six faces of the cubemap. The cubemap can either be saved as a single texture or split into individual face textures.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em fname} & Output file name or base name for the cubemap files. \\
\hline
{\em z} & Input 2D array representing the data to be converted into a cubemap. \\
\hline
{\em cubemap\+\_\+resolution} & Resolution (width and height) of each individual face of the cubemap. \\
\hline
{\em overlap} & Fraction (0 to 1) of overlap between adjacent faces to ensure smooth transitions. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius parameter for smoothing at triple corners. \\
\hline
{\em cmap} & Colormap to be applied when exporting the textures. \\
\hline
{\em splitted} & If true, exports each face of the cubemap as a separate image; otherwise, exports the entire cubemap as a single texture. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+cubemap} & Pointer to an optional output array where the final cubemap data will be stored.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
The generated cubemap maintains continuity between faces, adjusting values at overlapping regions and corners using smooth transitions. If the {\ttfamily splitted} flag is set, six individual PNG images are generated for the cubemap faces with appropriate suffixes appended to the base name. Otherwise, the entire cubemap is exported as a single texture file.

Exports a 2D array as a set of grayscale PNG image tiles. 

This function divides a given 2D array into smaller rectangular tiles and saves each tile as a grayscale PNG image file. Tiles are named using a combination of the provided file name radical, tile indices, and file extension.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em fname\+\_\+radical} & Base name (radical) for output image files. \\
\hline
{\em fname\+\_\+extension} & File extension to use for exported images (e.\+g., "{}png"{}). \\
\hline
{\em array} & The input 2D array to be tiled and exported. \\
\hline
{\em tiling} & A 2D vector specifying the number of tiles in the x and y directions. \\
\hline
{\em leading\+\_\+zeros} & Number of digits used to pad the tile indices in the filename. \\
\hline
{\em depth} & Bit depth of the output PNG images (commonly 8 or 16). \\
\hline
{\em overlapping\+\_\+edges} & If true, each tile includes an extra row/column from neighboring tiles (for overlap). \\
\hline
{\em reverse\+\_\+tile\+\_\+y\+\_\+indexing} & If true, Y tile indices are reversed (tile 0 is at the top).\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
Each tile is extracted using slicing, adjusted for overlap if specified, and then exported as an individual image file named with its tile indices. For example, an output file might be named {\ttfamily radical\+\_\+01\+\_\+03.\+png}.

Reads an image file and converts it to a 2D array. 

This function uses the Open\+CV {\ttfamily imread} function to load an image from the specified file. The supported file formats are those recognized by Open\+CV\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily imread} function, such as JPEG, PNG, BMP, and others. If the image is in color, it is automatically converted to grayscale using the built-\/in Open\+CV codec converter. This conversion process may introduce artifacts depending on the image\textquotesingle{}s original format and content.

Identifies and labels connected components within a binary or labeled array, with optional filtering by size. 

Connected-\/component labeling is a technique used to identify clusters of connected pixels (or components) in an array. This function can be used in image processing and spatial analysis to isolate regions of interest, such as detecting distinct objects or areas within a heightmap.

{\bfseries{Usage}}
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Use this function to label distinct features within an array, such as individual water bodies, forest patches, or elevation features.
\item Apply the surface threshold to filter out small, insignificant components that might be noise or irrelevant.
\end{DoxyItemize}


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The input array where connected components are to be identified. \\
\hline
{\em surface\+\_\+threshold} & The minimum number of pixels a component must have to be retained. Components smaller than this threshold will be removed. The default value is 0 (no filtering). \\
\hline
{\em background\+\_\+value} & The value used to represent background pixels, which are not part of any component. Default is 0. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

K-\/means clustering is a popular unsupervised learning algorithm used to partition data into clusters. This function applies k-\/means clustering to two arrays, which might represent different terrain attributes or environmental variables.

\begin{DoxyItemize}

\item Useful in ecological modeling, land cover classification, and resource management.

Performs k-\/means clustering on three input arrays, providing more detailed cluster analysis by considering an additional dimension. 

This version of k-\/means clustering includes a third array, enabling more complex clustering based on three terrain attributes or environmental variables.

{\bfseries{Usage}}
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Apply this function to analyze the relationships between three different terrain attributes, revealing complex patterns.
\item Useful in multi-\/dimensional environmental modeling and resource management.
\end{DoxyItemize}


\begin{DoxyParams}[1]{Parameters}
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em array1} & The first input array for clustering. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em array2} & The second input array for clustering. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em array3} & The third input array for clustering. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em nclusters} & The number of clusters (k) to be formed. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ out}}  & {\em p\+\_\+scoring} & (optional) A pointer to a vector of arrays where the clustering scores will be stored. Pass nullptr if scoring is not required. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ out}}  & {\em p\+\_\+aggregate\+\_\+scoring} & (optional) A pointer to an array where the aggregate score across all clusters will be stored. Pass nullptr if not required. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em weights} & A vector of three floats representing the weight given to {\ttfamily array1}, {\ttfamily array2}, and {\ttfamily array3}. The default weights are \{1.\+f, 1.\+f, 1.\+f\}. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em seed} & A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the clustering results. The default value is 1. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} An array representing the clustered data, with each pixel assigned to a cluster.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Expand heights outward from a masked region with a talus slope limit. 

Starting from the non-\/zero cells of {\ttfamily mask}, heights are propagated outward using a min-\/heap so lower cells are processed first. Neighbor heights are computed from the source height plus {\ttfamily dist \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} talus}, optionally perturbed with noise.

Intuition\+: grows terrain outward from seed cells, filling empty space while respecting a maximum slope.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Height array modified in-\/place. \\
\hline
{\em mask} & Initial region to expand from. \\
\hline
{\em talus} & Maximum slope per unit distance. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & RNG seed for noise. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Neighborhood radius. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+ratio} & Amplitude of slope noise. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\Hypertarget{namespacehmap_a9c26b60e353b42465e4ccaf8b3c6d2cb}\label{namespacehmap_a9c26b60e353b42465e4ccaf8b3c6d2cb}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{fill\_talus()}{fill\_talus()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::fill\+\_\+talus (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{z,  }\item[{float}]{talus,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{int}]{ir = {\ttfamily 1},  }\item[{float}]{noise\+\_\+ratio = {\ttfamily 0.2\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+seed\+\_\+mask = {\ttfamily nullptr} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Enforce a talus slope constraint on a height field. 

Cells are processed from highest to lowest using a max-\/heap. Each cell may raise neighboring cells so that the slope relative to the current cell does not exceed the local talus value.

Intuition\+: stabilizes an existing terrain by redistributing height so slopes do not exceed the talus limit (similar to talus erosion / relaxation but by adding material).


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & A reference to the 2D array representing the terrain heights. The function modifies this array in place to introduce talus slopes. \\
\hline
{\em talus} & The critical slope angle that determines where material will move from higher elevations to lower ones. Slopes steeper than this value will be flattened by material transport. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & The seed for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the noise effects in the talus formation process. The same seed will produce the same terrain modifications. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+ratio} & A parameter that controls the amount of randomness or noise introduced in the talus formation process. The default value is 0.\+2.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

This function applies a folding filter to the input array, where the values are successively folded (using absolute values) within a specified range, defined by {\ttfamily vmin} and {\ttfamily vmax}. The process can be repeated for a number of iterations, with an optional smoothing parameter {\ttfamily k} to control the intensity of the folding effect.

\hline
{\em iterations} & Number of iterations for applying the folding filter. The default is 3. \\

Applies the Kuwahara filter to an array with optional per-\/pixel masking. 

This overloaded version of the Kuwahara filter allows applying the filter with a per-\/pixel mask. The mask determines the blending ratio for each pixel, allowing selective smoothing.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The input/output array to apply the filter on. The array is modified in place. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & The radius of the region to analyze for each pixel. Larger values result in stronger smoothing. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & A pointer to an array representing the mask. The values in the mask range from 0.\+0 to 1.\+0, specifying the blending ratio for each pixel. If {\ttfamily nullptr}, the filter is applied without masking. \\
\hline
{\em mix\+\_\+ratio} & A blending factor between the original and filtered arrays when {\ttfamily p\+\_\+mask} is {\ttfamily nullptr}. Ignored if {\ttfamily p\+\_\+mask} is provided.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
If no mask is provided\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The function behaves like the single-\/argument version of {\ttfamily kuwahara}.
\end{DoxyItemize}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::laplace (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{float}]{sigma = {\ttfamily 0.125\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{int}]{iterations = {\ttfamily 3} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Applies an iterative 8-\/neighbor Laplacian smoothing filter on an array. 

This function performs isotropic Laplacian diffusion on a 2D array using an explicit finite-\/difference scheme. Each cell is updated according to the local Laplacian computed from its 8 surrounding neighbors\+:

\[
A_{i,j}^{t+1} = A_{i,j}^{t} + \sigma \cdot
\left( \sum_{(p,q)\in N_{8}(i,j)} A_{p,q}^{t} - 8A_{i,j}^{t} \right)
\]

where ( N\+\_\+\{8\}(i,j) ) denotes the 8 neighboring cells.

Boundary cells are handled by clamping neighbor indices to the valid range, effectively replicating edge values at the borders.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The 2D array to be smoothed (modified in place). \\
\hline
{\em sigma} & Diffusion coefficient (small positive value, e.\+g. 0.\+05–0.25). \\
\hline
{\em iterations} & Number of diffusion iterations to apply.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply a low-\/pass Laplace filter with a mask. 

This overload applies the Laplace filter to the input array using an optional mask. The mask determines which parts of the array are affected by the filter. The filtering intensity and the number of iterations control the extent of the smoothing effect.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array to which the Laplace filter is applied. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the array are affected by the filter. \\
\hline
{\em sigma} & Filtering intensity, expected to be in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. It controls the strength of the filtering effect. A value closer to 1 results in more smoothing. The default value is 0.\+2. \\
\hline
{\em iterations} & Number of iterations to apply the filter. More iterations will increase the smoothing effect. The default value is 3.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\hline

Apply a low-\/pass anisotropic Laplace filter to the input array. 

This function applies an anisotropic Laplace filter to the input array. Anisotropic diffusion, also known as edge-\/preserving smoothing, helps to reduce noise while preserving edges. The effect of the filter is controlled by the talus limit, filtering intensity, and the number of iterations.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array to which the anisotropic Laplace filter is applied. \\
\hline
{\em talus} & Talus limit for edge sensitivity. Gradients above this value are less affected by the filtering, preserving important edges in the data. \\
\hline
{\em sigma} & Filtering intensity, expected to be in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. It controls the strength of the filtering effect. A value closer to 1 results in more smoothing. The default value is 0.\+2. \\
\hline
{\em iterations} & Number of iterations to apply the filter. More iterations will increase the smoothing effect. The default value is 3.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Applies the mean shift algorithm to the input array. 

The mean shift algorithm iteratively adjusts each value in the input array by averaging nearby values within a specified radius ({\ttfamily ir}), using either simple or weighted mean computation. The process stops after the specified number of iterations or if convergence criteria are met.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The input array to process. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & The radius of the neighborhood to consider for mean computation. \\
\hline
{\em threshold} & The value threshold for considering neighboring elements. Only elements with differences below this threshold are included. \\
\hline
{\em iterations} & The number of iterations to perform the mean shift process. \\
\hline
{\em talus\+\_\+weighted} & If true, uses weighted mean based on differences between values and their neighbors. If false, uses unweighted mean. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new array containing the result of the mean shift process.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Computes a fast pseudo-\/median approximation of a local neighborhood in an array. 

This function approximates the effect of a median filter by computing the local minimum, maximum, and mean values within a square neighborhood of radius {\ttfamily ir}, and averaging the results\+:

\[
\text{pseudo\_median}(x, y) = \frac{\text{min} + \text{max} + \text{mean}}{3}
\]

This method is computationally cheaper than a true median filter and can approximate its noise-\/reduction and edge-\/preserving properties to some extent.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array (e.\+g., image or 2D signal). \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius of the square neighborhood (kernel size will be $2
              \cdot ir + 1$). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
An \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} containing the pseudo-\/median filtered output.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
This method works best on images with impulsive noise (e.\+g., salt-\/and-\/pepper), but is only an approximation and may behave differently from a true median filter on complex structures or edges.
\end{DoxyNote}

Apply a plateau-\/shape filter to the input array. 

This function applies a plateau-\/shape filter to the input array, modifying the terrain to create flat, plateau-\/like regions. The filter\textquotesingle{}s radius and flatness can be adjusted to control the extent and shape of the plateaus. An optional mask can be used to control which parts of the array are affected.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array to which the plateau-\/shape filter is applied. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the array are affected by the filter. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Plateau radius. The size of the area over which the plateau effect is applied. \\
\hline
{\em factor} & Gain factor that controls the flatness of the plateau. The higher the factor, the flatter the resulting plateau. The default value is 1.\+0.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Transform heightmap to give a "{}billow"{} like appearance. 

This function modifies the heightmap to produce a "{}billow"{} effect. The transformation is applied based on a reference elevation ({\ttfamily vref}) where the elevation is folded. The smoothing coefficient ({\ttfamily k}) controls the degree of smoothing applied during the transformation.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be transformed. \\
\hline
{\em vref} & Reference elevation where the heightmap values are folded. This value determines the baseline around which the billow effect is centered. \\
\hline
{\em k} & Smoothing coefficient that influences the degree of smoothness in the billow transformation. Higher values result in more smoothing.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

This function modifies the heightmap to create a "{}canyon"{} effect. The transformation is based on a canyon top elevation ({\ttfamily vcut}). The effect can be adjusted with a gamma factor to control the intensity of the canyon effect. Optional parameters include a filter mask for selective application and a noise array for additional variation.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be transformed. \\
\hline
{\em vcut} & Canyon top elevation. This value defines the threshold for canyon formation. \\
\hline
{\em gamma} & Gamma factor (\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 0) that adjusts the intensity of the canyon effect. A higher value increases the effect. The default value is 4.\+0. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the heightmap are affected by the transformation. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise} & Optional noise array used to introduce variation in the canyon effect. If not provided, no additional noise is applied.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{recast\_cliff()}{recast\_cliff()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::recast\+\_\+cliff (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{float}]{talus,  }\item[{int}]{ir,  }\item[{float}]{amplitude,  }\item[{float}]{gain = {\ttfamily 2.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Transform heightmap to add cliffs where gradients are steep enough. 

This function modifies the heightmap to introduce cliffs based on a reference talus angle. Cliffs are added where the gradient exceeds the specified talus angle. The amplitude of the cliffs and the gain factor for steepness are adjustable. Additionally, a filter mask can be applied to control which parts of the heightmap are affected.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be modified. \\
\hline
{\em talus} & Reference talus angle. This angle determines the threshold above which cliffs are formed. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Filter radius used to smooth the heightmap before applying the cliff effect. \\
\hline
{\em amplitude} & Amplitude of the cliffs. This value controls the height of the cliffs. \\
\hline
{\em gain} & Gain factor for the gain filter, influencing the steepness of the cliffs. Higher values result in steeper cliffs. The default value is 2.\+0. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the heightmap are affected by the cliff transformation.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{recast\_cliff\_directional()}{recast\_cliff\_directional()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::recast\+\_\+cliff\+\_\+directional (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{float}]{talus,  }\item[{int}]{ir,  }\item[{float}]{amplitude,  }\item[{float}]{angle,  }\item[{float}]{gain = {\ttfamily 2.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Transform heightmap to add directional cliffs where gradients are steep enough. 

This function modifies the heightmap to introduce cliffs in a specific direction, based on a reference talus angle. The cliffs are added where the gradient exceeds the specified talus angle, with the direction of the cliffs controlled by the specified angle. The amplitude of the cliffs and the gain factor for steepness are also adjustable. A filter mask can be used to specify which parts of the heightmap are affected.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be modified. \\
\hline
{\em talus} & Reference talus angle. This angle determines the threshold above which cliffs are formed. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Filter radius used to smooth the heightmap before applying the cliff effect. \\
\hline
{\em amplitude} & Amplitude of the cliffs. This value controls the height of the cliffs. \\
\hline
{\em angle} & Angle (in degrees) determining the direction of the cliffs. \\
\hline
{\em gain} & Gain factor for the gain filter, influencing the steepness of the cliffs. Higher values result in steeper cliffs. The default value is 2.\+0. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the heightmap are affected by the cliff transformation.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{recast\_escarpment()}{recast\_escarpment()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::recast\+\_\+escarpment (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{int}]{ir = {\ttfamily 16},  }\item[{float}]{ratio = {\ttfamily 0.1\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{float}]{scale = {\ttfamily 1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{bool}]{reverse = {\ttfamily false},  }\item[{bool}]{transpose\+\_\+effect = {\ttfamily false},  }\item[{float}]{global\+\_\+scaling = {\ttfamily 0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Applies an escarpment effect to the given 2D array, modifying its values based on cumulative displacement with optional directional and transpositional transformations. 

This function calculates cumulative displacement along the x-\/axis based on relative elevation differences between adjacent cells. The displacement is scaled and optionally reversed, then used to apply a warping effect to the array, simulating an escarpment feature. An optional global scaling factor can further adjust the displacement effect intensity.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Reference to the 2D array where the escarpment effect will be applied. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius for the smoothing kernel used on the displacement, controlling the smoothness of the effect. Larger values result in smoother transitions. \\
\hline
{\em ratio} & The ratio influencing displacement; values \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 1.\+0 increase displacement sensitivity to height differences. \\
\hline
{\em scale} & The scaling factor for the cumulative displacement, affecting the intensity of the effect. \\
\hline
{\em reverse} & If true, reverses the direction of the displacement effect. \\
\hline
{\em transpose\+\_\+effect} & If true, transposes the array before and after applying the effect. \\
\hline
{\em global\+\_\+scaling} & An additional scaling factor for the displacement; if set to 0, a default value is computed based on the array\textquotesingle{}s range and size. Higher values increase the overall effect.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{recast\_escarpment()}{recast\_escarpment()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [2/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::recast\+\_\+escarpment (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+mask,  }\item[{int}]{ir = {\ttfamily 16},  }\item[{float}]{ratio = {\ttfamily 0.1\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{float}]{scale = {\ttfamily 1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{bool}]{reverse = {\ttfamily false},  }\item[{bool}]{transpose\+\_\+effect = {\ttfamily false},  }\item[{float}]{global\+\_\+scaling = {\ttfamily 0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Applies an escarpment effect to the given 2D array, with an optional mask to blend the effect. 

This overload allows for a blending mask that controls the intensity of the escarpment effect at each point in the array. The mask values range between 0 and 1, where values closer to 1 fully apply the effect, and values closer to 0 reduce it. An optional global scaling factor can further adjust the displacement effect intensity.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Reference to the 2D array where the escarpment effect will be applied. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Pointer to an optional mask array for blending the effect, where values range from 0 to 1. A nullptr applies the effect fully without blending. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius for the smoothing kernel used on the displacement, controlling the smoothness of the effect. Larger values result in smoother transitions. \\
\hline
{\em ratio} & The ratio influencing displacement; values \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 1.\+0 increase displacement sensitivity to height differences. \\
\hline
{\em scale} & The scaling factor for the cumulative displacement, affecting the intensity of the effect. \\
\hline
{\em reverse} & If true, reverses the direction of the displacement effect. \\
\hline
{\em transpose\+\_\+effect} & If true, transposes the array before and after applying the effect. \\
\hline
{\em global\+\_\+scaling} & An additional scaling factor for the displacement; if set to 0, a default value is computed based on the array\textquotesingle{}s range and size. Higher values increase the overall effect.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

{\bfseries{Result}}  \Hypertarget{namespacehmap_ac2a2b604d4c167dcaddfbd1c66df3e4c}\label{namespacehmap_ac2a2b604d4c167dcaddfbd1c66df3e4c} 
\index{hmap@{hmap}!recast\_peak@{recast\_peak}}
\index{recast\_peak@{recast\_peak}!hmap@{hmap}}
\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{recast\_peak()}{recast\_peak()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::recast\+\_\+peak (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{int}]{ir,  }\item[{float}]{gamma = {\ttfamily 2.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{float}]{k = {\ttfamily 0.1\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Transform heightmap to give a "{}peak"{} like appearance. 

This function modifies the heightmap to create a "{}peak"{} effect, where the elevations are adjusted to emphasize peak-\/like features. The transformation is applied based on a filter radius ({\ttfamily ir}) and involves gamma correction and smoothing parameters. The effect can be selectively applied using a filter mask.

\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} values are expected to be in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}.
\end{DoxyWarning}

\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be transformed. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Filter radius used to smooth the heightmap before applying the peak effect. \\
\hline
{\em gamma} & Gamma factor (\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 0) that adjusts the intensity of the peak effect. A higher value increases the effect. The default value is 2.\+0. For details on gamma correction, see {\ttfamily \doxylink{namespacehmap_aba3674787d520af15267ee7d1e46d220}{gamma\+\_\+correction}}. \\
\hline
{\em k} & Smoothing parameter (\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 0) that controls the degree of smoothing applied during the transformation. Higher values result in more smoothing. The default value is 0.\+1. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the heightmap are affected by the peak transformation.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::recast\+\_\+rocky\+\_\+slopes (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{float}]{talus,  }\item[{int}]{ir,  }\item[{float}]{amplitude,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{float}]{kw,  }\item[{float}]{gamma = {\ttfamily 0.5\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+noise = {\ttfamily nullptr},  }\item[{glm\+::vec4}]{bbox = {\ttfamily \{0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}\}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Transform heightmap by adding "{}rock-\/like"{} features at higher slopes. 

This function modifies the heightmap to introduce rock-\/like features, particularly at locations with higher slopes. The transformation is controlled by parameters defining talus limit, filter radius, amplitude, and noise characteristics. The rock features are generated using a specified random seed and can be customized with optional noise and gamma correction. A filter mask can be applied to control which parts of the heightmap are affected.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be transformed. \\
\hline
{\em talus} & Talus limit that determines the threshold above which rock-\/like features are introduced based on slope steepness. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Filter radius used to smooth the heightmap and define the area of influence for adding rock features. \\
\hline
{\em amplitude} & Amplitude of the rock features. This value controls the intensity of the rock-\/like appearance. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random number seed used to generate noise patterns for the rock features. Different seeds produce different rock patterns. \\
\hline
{\em kw} & Noise wavenumber with respect to a unit domain, influencing the frequency of rock features. Higher values result in more detailed rock textures. \\
\hline
{\em gamma} & Gamma correction coefficient applied to the rock features. This parameter adjusts the contrast of the rock features. The default value is 0.\+5. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise} & Optional reference to an input noise array used for generating rock features. If provided, it overrides the default noise generator. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the heightmap are affected by the rock feature transformation. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box defining the region of interest within the heightmap. This parameter specifies the coordinates of the bounding box in the format \{xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax\}. The default bounding box covers the entire domain.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{recast\_sag()}{recast\_sag()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::recast\+\_\+sag (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{float}]{vref,  }\item[{float}]{k }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Transform heightmap to give a "{}cliff"{} like appearance. 

This function modifies the heightmap to create a "{}cliff"{} effect by folding the elevations around a reference height ({\ttfamily vref}). The transformation is influenced by a smoothing coefficient ({\ttfamily k}) and can be selectively applied using a filter mask.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be transformed. \\
\hline
{\em vref} & Reference elevation where the heightmap is folded to create the cliff-\/like appearance. Elevations near this value will be prominently altered. \\
\hline
{\em k} & Smoothing coefficient that controls the degree of smoothing applied during the transformation. A higher value results in smoother cliffs. The default value is not specified in this function; it must be provided by the user. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the heightmap are affected by the cliff transformation. If not provided, the transformation is applied to the entire heightmap.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
