\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{recurve()}{recurve()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::recurve (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{const std\+::vector$<$ float $>$ \&}]{t,  }\item[{const std\+::vector$<$ float $>$ \&}]{v }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Apply a curve adjustment filter to the array. 

This function applies a curve adjustment to the heightmap by mapping input values to output values according to a given correction curve. The curve is monotonically interpolated, and any values outside the defined input range are clipped. The filter can be selectively applied using a mask.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be adjusted. \\
\hline
{\em t} & Vector of input values for the correction curve. These values define the x-\/coordinates (input values) of the curve. \\
\hline
{\em v} & Vector of output values for the correction curve. These values define the y-\/coordinates (output values) of the curve corresponding to the input values in {\ttfamily t}. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the heightmap are affected by the curve adjustment. If not provided, the curve adjustment is applied to the entire heightmap.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply a curve adjustment filter using a "{}bumpy exponential-\/shape"{} curve. 

This function adjusts the heightmap using a "{}bumpy exponential-\/shape"{} curve, where the curve has an exponential decay defined by the parameter {\ttfamily tau}. The curve transformation is applied to the entire heightmap or selectively using a filter mask.

\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} values are expected to be in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}.
\end{DoxyWarning}

\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be adjusted. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. The mask specifies which parts of the heightmap are affected by the curve adjustment. If not provided, the adjustment is applied to the entire heightmap. \\
\hline
{\em tau} & Exponential decay parameter that defines the shape of the "{}bumpy"{} curve. Higher values of {\ttfamily tau} result in a sharper curve. The default value is 0.\+5.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply a curve adjustment filter using Kumaraswamy\textquotesingle{}s cumulative distribution function (CDF). 

This function transforms the heightmap using Kumaraswamy\textquotesingle{}s CDF, which is defined by two shape parameters, {\ttfamily a} and {\ttfamily b}. The transformation applies a curve adjustment that can shape the data closer to 0 or 1 depending on the values of {\ttfamily a} and {\ttfamily b}. The adjustment can be applied to the entire heightmap or selectively using a filter mask.

\hline
{\em b} & Parameter \textquotesingle{}b\textquotesingle{} of Kumaraswamy\textquotesingle{}s CDF, which drives the curve shape towards 1. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If provided, the adjustment is applied according to this mask. If not provided, the entire heightmap is adjusted.\\

Apply a curve adjustment filter using an nth-\/order smoothstep curve. 

This function applies a curve adjustment to the heightmap using a smoothstep function of order {\ttfamily n}. The smoothstep function provides a smooth transition between 0 and 1, where {\ttfamily n} determines the smoothness of the transition. The adjustment can be applied to the entire heightmap or selectively using a filter mask.

\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} values are expected to be in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}.
\end{DoxyWarning}

\hline

\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, with values expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If provided, the adjustment is applied according to this mask. If not provided, the entire heightmap is adjusted.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Applies a smooth reversal of values above a given threshold. 

This function modifies the elements of an array by "{}reversing"{} values that exceed a given threshold value, optionally blending the effect over a transition range.

For values above the threshold\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The difference between the value and the threshold is scaled down proportionally to {\ttfamily scaling} and modulated by a smooth transition (using smoothstep3) based on {\ttfamily transition\+\_\+extent}.
\end{DoxyItemize}

For values below the threshold\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The values are linearly blended ({\ttfamily lerp}) with the threshold value using a smooth transition factor, gradually reducing the reversal effect.
\end{DoxyItemize}


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} to modify in place. \\
\hline
{\em threshold} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} containing the per-\/element threshold values. \\
\hline
{\em scaling} & Multiplier applied to the difference above the threshold. \\
\hline
{\em transition\+\_\+extent} & Width of the smooth transition zone for blending.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\hline

\hline

Apply a sharpening filter based on the Laplace operator. 

This function applies a sharpening filter to the input array using the Laplace operator. The sharpening effect can be controlled by adjusting the {\ttfamily ratio} parameter, which determines the balance between the sharpened and non-\/sharpened output. A {\ttfamily ratio} of 1 applies full sharpening, while a {\ttfamily ratio} of 0 applies no sharpening.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap or image to be sharpened. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If provided, sharpening is applied according to this mask. If not provided, the entire array is sharpened. \\
\hline
{\em ratio} & Ratio of the sharpening effect. A value of 1 applies full sharpening, while a value of 0 applies no sharpening. Default is 1.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply a sharpening filter based on a smooth cone filter. 

This function applies a sharpening filter to the input array using a smooth cone filter. The sharpening effect can be controlled by the {\ttfamily scale} parameter, and the size of the smoothing operation is determined by the {\ttfamily ir} parameter. The optional filter mask allows selective application of the sharpening effect.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap or image to be sharpened. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If provided, sharpening is applied according to this mask. If not provided, the entire array is sharpened. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Filter radius, which determines the size of the smoothing operation. \\
\hline
{\em scale} & Sharpening scale. Adjusts the intensity of the sharpening effect. Default is 0.\+5.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply shrinking, or "{}deflating"{}, to emphasize the ridges in the heightmap. 

This function applies a shrinking filter to the input array, which accentuates the ridges by shrinking or deflating the terrain features. The filter radius {\ttfamily ir} determines the extent of the deflation. You can also apply the shrinking effect selectively using an optional filter mask. Additionally, an alternative method using a custom kernel is available.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap to be processed. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Filter radius, which controls the extent of the shrinking effect. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If provided, shrinking is applied according to this mask. If not provided, the entire array is processed. \\
\hline
{\em kernel} & Optional custom kernel to be used for the shrinking operation. If provided, this kernel will override the default filter radius.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply directional shrinking, or "{}deflating"{}, to emphasize the ridges in the terrain. 

This function applies a directional shrinking filter to the input array, enhancing the ridges by shrinking or deflating the terrain features with respect to a specified direction. Parameters include filter radius {\ttfamily ir}, direction angle, aspect ratio, and anisotropy to control the shape and orientation of the filter. An optional filter mask can be used for selective application.

\hline

\hline
{\em angle} & Angle (in degrees) of the directional filter. \\
\hline
{\em aspect\+\_\+ratio} & Pulse aspect ratio, which influences the shape of the filter. \\
\hline
{\em anisotropy} & Pulse width ratio between upstream and downstream sides. Default is 1. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If provided, shrinking is applied according to this mask. If not provided, the entire array is processed.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply filtering to the array using convolution with a cubic pulse kernel. 

This function performs convolution on the input array using a cubic pulse kernel. It serves as an alternative to Gaussian smoothing, offering a more compact support with potentially faster computations. For direct comparison with Gaussian smoothing, the pulse radius {\ttfamily ir} should be set to twice the desired Gaussian half-\/width.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap or image to be smoothed. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Pulse radius, where the half-\/width of the cubic pulse kernel is half of this value. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If provided, filtering is applied according to this mask. If not provided, the entire array is processed.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Smooths an array while attenuating edges using a gradient-\/based pulse. 

This function first computes the gradient norm of the input array, applies a sigmoid filter to highlight or attenuate regions based on the local gradient magnitude, and then performs a constrained pulse smoothing pass that respects those gradient-\/based weights. This is useful for smoothing heightmaps or scalar fields while preserving significant edges such as ridges or cliffs.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Reference to the input array to be smoothed. The array is modified in-\/place. \\
\hline
{\em talus} & Threshold value used in the sigmoid function to control where edge attenuation starts. Lower values affect more regions. \\
\hline
{\em talus\+\_\+width} & Width (steepness) of the sigmoid transition zone around the talus threshold. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius of the smoothing kernel used in the constrained pulse smoothing step. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Applies a smoothing average filter to the given 2D array in both dimensions. 

This function creates a smoothing kernel of size (2 \textbackslash{}times \textbackslash{}text\{ir\} + 1) with uniform weights, then applies a 1D convolution along both the i (rows) and j (columns) dimensions of the array to achieve a 2D smoothing effect.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Reference to the 2D array to be smoothed. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius of the smoothing kernel, determining its size as (2 \textbackslash{}times \textbackslash{}text\{ir\} + 1). Larger values produce more smoothing. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply Gaussian filtering to the array. 

This function performs convolution on the input array using a Gaussian kernel, which smooths the array by averaging values within a Gaussian-\/weighted neighborhood. The {\ttfamily ir} parameter specifies the Gaussian half-\/width, which influences the extent of the smoothing effect. An optional filter mask can be provided for selective filtering.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array representing the heightmap or image to be smoothed. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Gaussian half-\/width, which determines the extent of the smoothing effect. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If provided, filtering is applied according to this mask. If not provided, the entire array is processed.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Apply cubic pulse smoothing to fill lower flat regions while preserving some sharpness. 

This function applies a cubic pulse smoothing technique to the input array, specifically designed to fill in lower flat regions without significantly impacting sharp features. It provides a more computationally efficient alternative to the {\ttfamily thermal\+\_\+auto\+\_\+bedrock} method. The {\ttfamily p\+\_\+deposition\+\_\+map} output field captures the amount of smoothing applied.

\hline

This function applies a nonlinear convection operator to the input array, simulating the effect described by Burger\textquotesingle{}s equation. The steepening effect is applied in the specified direction (angle) and is controlled by several parameters including the number of iterations, smoothing radius, and time step. The input array values are expected to be in the range \mbox{[}-\/1, 1\mbox{]}.

\hline
{\em ir} & Smoothing radius applied to the array values before differentiation. \\
\hline
{\em dt} & Time step for the convection process, can be chosen smaller than 1 for finer tuning of the steepening effect. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional filter mask, expected in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. If provided, steepening is applied according to this mask. If not provided, the entire array is processed.\\

Applies a terrace effect to the values in an array. 

This function adjusts the values in the {\ttfamily array} by applying a terrace or stepped effect, often used for terrain generation or other natural-\/looking height variations. The terrace effect is controlled by several parameters such as the number of levels, gain, noise ratio, and optional min/max range. The noise is applied to levels for added randomness, and a gain function is applied to smooth the transitions.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The array of values to modify with the terrace effect. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Seed value for random number generation. \\
\hline
{\em nlevels} & Number of terrace levels to apply. \\
\hline
{\em gain} & Gain factor for controlling the sharpness of the terrace levels, in \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of noise applied to each terrace level, except the first and last. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise} & Optional noise array to introduce additional variation per element. \\
\hline
{\em vmin} & Minimum value for terracing; if less than {\ttfamily vmax}, will be auto-\/determined. \\
\hline
{\em vmax} & Maximum value for terracing; if less than {\ttfamily vmin}, will be auto-\/determined.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
If {\ttfamily p\+\_\+noise} is provided, each value in {\ttfamily array} is transformed using both the original value and the corresponding noise value from {\ttfamily p\+\_\+noise}.
\end{DoxyNote}

Applies a terrace effect to an array with optional masking. 

This overloaded version of the terrace function modifies {\ttfamily array} based on the terrace levels, gain, noise ratio, and an optional mask array. If a mask is provided, the terrace effect is applied conditionally based on the mask values.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The array of values to modify with the terrace effect. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Seed value for random number generation. \\
\hline
{\em nlevels} & Number of terrace levels to apply. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional mask array. If provided, blends the terrace effect with original values based on the mask. \\
\hline
{\em gain} & Gain factor for controlling the sharpness of the terrace levels, in \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of noise applied to each terrace level, except the first and last. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise} & Optional noise array to introduce additional variation per element. \\
\hline
{\em vmin} & Minimum value for terracing; if less than {\ttfamily vmax}, will be auto-\/determined. \\
\hline
{\em vmax} & Maximum value for terracing; if less than {\ttfamily vmin}, will be auto-\/determined.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
This function\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item If no mask is provided, directly applies the terrace effect using the first terrace overload.
\item If a mask is provided, creates a temporary copy of {\ttfamily array}, applies the terrace effect to it, and then interpolates between {\ttfamily array} and the modified copy based on mask values.
\end{DoxyItemize}

\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The mask array allows for blending the terrace effect with the original array for more localized effects.
\end{DoxyNote}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{random\_cloud\_density()}{random\_cloud\_density()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud}} hmap\+::random\+\_\+cloud\+\_\+density (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{size\+\_\+t}]{count,  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{density,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{const glm\+::vec4 \&}]{bbox = {\ttfamily \{0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}\}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Generates a random cloud of points based on a spatial density map. 

The probability of placing a point at a location is proportional to the density value at that location.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em count} & Number of points to generate. \\
\hline
{\em density} & 2D array representing spatial density values. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random number generator seed. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box in which to generate the points (a,b,c,d = xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax). Defaults to the unit square \{0.\+f, 1.\+f, 0.\+f, 1.\+f\}. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud} containing the generated points.
\end{DoxyReturn}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud}} hmap\+::random\+\_\+cloud\+\_\+distance (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{float}]{min\+\_\+dist,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{const glm\+::vec4 \&}]{bbox = {\ttfamily \{0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}\}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Generates a random cloud of points separated by at least a given minimum distance. 

Points are distributed randomly but maintain a minimum separation, producing a blue-\/noise-\/like distribution.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em min\+\_\+dist} & Minimum allowed distance between any two points. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random number generator seed. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box in which to generate the points (a,b,c,d = xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax). Defaults to the unit square \{0.\+f, 1.\+f, 0.\+f, 1.\+f\}. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud} containing the generated points.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{random\_cloud\_distance()}{random\_cloud\_distance()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [2/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud}} hmap\+::random\+\_\+cloud\+\_\+distance (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{float}]{min\+\_\+dist,  }\item[{float}]{max\+\_\+dist,  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{density,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{const glm\+::vec4 \&}]{bbox = {\ttfamily \{0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}\}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Generates a random cloud of points separated by a distance range, influenced by a density map. 

Points maintain a separation between {\ttfamily min\+\_\+dist} and {\ttfamily max\+\_\+dist}, and are distributed according to the provided density map.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em min\+\_\+dist} & Minimum allowed distance between points. \\
\hline
{\em max\+\_\+dist} & Maximum allowed distance between points. \\
\hline
{\em density} & 2D array representing spatial density values. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random number generator seed. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box in which to generate the points (a,b,c,d = xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax). Defaults to the unit square \{0.\+f, 1.\+f, 0.\+f, 1.\+f\}. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud} containing the generated points.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{random\_cloud\_distance\_power\_law()}{random\_cloud\_distance\_power\_law()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud}} hmap\+::random\+\_\+cloud\+\_\+distance\+\_\+power\+\_\+law (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{float}]{dist\+\_\+min,  }\item[{float}]{dist\+\_\+max,  }\item[{float}]{alpha,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{const glm\+::vec4 \&}]{bbox = {\ttfamily \{0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}\}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Generates a random cloud of points with distances drawn from a power-\/law distribution. 

Distances between points follow a power-\/law distribution between {\ttfamily dist\+\_\+min} and {\ttfamily dist\+\_\+max}, with exponent {\ttfamily alpha}.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em dist\+\_\+min} & Minimum possible distance between points. \\
\hline
{\em dist\+\_\+max} & Maximum possible distance between points. \\
\hline
{\em alpha} & Power-\/law exponent (larger alpha favors shorter distances). \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random number generator seed. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box in which to generate the points (a,b,c,d = xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax). Defaults to the unit square \{0.\+f, 1.\+f, 0.\+f, 1.\+f\}. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud} containing the generated points.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{random\_cloud\_distance\_weibull()}{random\_cloud\_distance\_weibull()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud}} hmap\+::random\+\_\+cloud\+\_\+distance\+\_\+weibull (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{float}]{dist\+\_\+min,  }\item[{float}]{lambda,  }\item[{float}]{k,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{const glm\+::vec4 \&}]{bbox = {\ttfamily \{0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}\}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Generates a random cloud of points with distances drawn from a Weibull distribution. 

Distances between points follow a Weibull distribution parameterized by {\ttfamily lambda} (scale) and {\ttfamily k} (shape).


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em dist\+\_\+min} & Minimum possible distance between points. \\
\hline
{\em lambda} & Weibull distribution scale parameter. \\
\hline
{\em k} & Weibull distribution shape parameter. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random number generator seed. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box in which to generate the points (a,b,c,d = xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax). Defaults to the unit square \{0.\+f, 1.\+f, 0.\+f, 1.\+f\}. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud} containing the generated points.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Generates a jittered grid cloud of points. 

Points are placed on a grid and then offset by a jitter amount, optionally staggered for a more irregular pattern.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em count} & Number of points to generate. \\
\hline
{\em jitter\+\_\+amount} & Maximum jitter to apply in each axis (x, y). \\
\hline
{\em stagger\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of staggering between consecutive rows or columns. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random number generator seed. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box in which to generate the points (a,b,c,d = xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax). Defaults to the unit square \{0.\+f, 1.\+f, 0.\+f, 1.\+f\}. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud} containing the generated points.
\end{DoxyReturn}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::rejection\+\_\+filter\+\_\+density (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Cloud}{Cloud}} \&}]{cloud,  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{density\+\_\+mask,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{const glm\+::vec4 \&}]{bbox = {\ttfamily \{0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}},~1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}\}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Filter a point cloud using rejection sampling based on a density mask. 

Each point in the input cloud is retained or discarded according to a spatially varying probability derived from the provided 2D density mask. The mask is mapped to the bounding box and evaluated as a continuous function over the domain.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em density\+\_\+mask} & 2D array defining the spatial density field over the bounding box. Values should lie in $[0,1]$. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed used for reproducible rejection sampling. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box {\ttfamily (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)} defining the spatial extent of the density mask in world coordinates. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Converts a length value to a pixel index in a discretized space. 

This function maps a floating-\/point length {\ttfamily x} to an integer pixel index, considering the total number of pixels {\ttfamily nx} and a scaling factor {\ttfamily scale}. Optionally, it can enforce lower and upper limits on the output index.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em x} & The length value to be converted. \\
\hline
{\em nx} & The number of pixels in the discretized space. \\
\hline
{\em lim\+\_\+inf} & If nonzero, enforces a minimum index of 1. \\
\hline
{\em lim\+\_\+sup} & If nonzero, enforces a maximum index of {\ttfamily nx -\/ 1}. \\
\hline
{\em scale} & The scaling factor relating the length to the pixel space. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
The computed pixel index. 
\end{DoxyReturn}

Smooth the path using Bezier curves. 

This method applies Bezier curve smoothing to the path. The {\ttfamily curvature\+\_\+ratio} controls the amount of curvature applied, with typical values in the range of \mbox{[}-\/1, 1\mbox{]}, where positive values generally result in more pronounced curvature. The {\ttfamily edge\+\_\+divisions} parameter determines the number of subdivisions per edge to create a smoother curve.

This method smooths the path using B-\/\+Spline curves, which provide a smooth curve that passes through the control points. The {\ttfamily edge\+\_\+divisions} parameter defines the number of subdivisions per edge for achieving smooth curves.

Smooth the path using De Casteljau curves. 

This function smooths a path by applying De Casteljau\textquotesingle{}s algorithm to generate intermediate points along the path, effectively creating a Bézier curve that approximates the original path. The path is divided into segments, and the De Casteljau algorithm is applied to each segment, resulting in a smooth curve.

The parameter {\ttfamily edge\+\_\+divisions} controls the number of divisions (sub-\/segments) created along each segment of the path. A higher number of divisions will result in a smoother curve, but will also increase the computational cost.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em edge\+\_\+divisions} & The number of divisions for each edge of the path. Default is 10, which provides a balanced level of smoothing. \\
\hline
{\em edm} & Mode for dividing edges (default is EDM\+\_\+\+PER\+\_\+\+EDGE).\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Applies fractalization to the path by adding points and randomly displacing their positions. 

This method enhances the complexity of a path by iteratively adding new points between existing ones and displacing them using Gaussian noise. The process can simulate natural phenomena like terrain generation or random walk paths. The number of iterations determines the level of detail added to the path.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em path} & The input path to be fractalized. \\
\hline
{\em iterations} & Number of iterations to apply the fractalization process. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility. \\
\hline
{\em sigma} & Standard deviation of the Gaussian displacement, relative to the distance between points. \\
\hline
{\em orientation} & Determines the displacement direction\+: {\ttfamily 0} for random, {\ttfamily 1} for inflation, {\ttfamily -\/1} for deflation. \\
\hline
{\em persistence} & Factor that adjusts the noise intensity across iterations. \\
\hline
{\em control\+\_\+field} & Optional pointer to an array that locally modifies the displacement amplitude. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box that defines the valid area for the control field\textquotesingle{}s influence. \\
\hline
{\em bounded} & If true, clamps each newly displaced midpoint to the bounding box defined by the initial edge it belongs to. Defaults to false.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Add "{}meanders"{} to the path. 

This method introduces meandering effects to the path by adding random deviations. The amplitude of the meanders is controlled by the {\ttfamily ratio} parameter, while the {\ttfamily noise\+\_\+ratio} controls the amount of randomness. The {\ttfamily seed} parameter is used to initialize the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility. The {\ttfamily iterations} parameter defines how many times the meandering process is applied, and {\ttfamily edge\+\_\+divisions} controls how finely each edge is subdivided during the meandering.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em path} & The input path to be meanderized. \\
\hline
{\em ratio} & Amplitude ratio of the meanders. Typically a positive value. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of randomness introduced during meandering. Default is 0.\+1. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Seed for random number generation. Default is 1. \\
\hline
{\em iterations} & Number of iterations to apply meandering. Default is 1. \\
\hline
{\em edge\+\_\+divisions} & Number of sub-\/divisions of each edge. Default is 10. \\
\hline
{\em edm} & The mode for dividing edges during the meandering process. Default is EDM\+\_\+\+PER\+\_\+\+EDGE.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

This function iteratively detects self-\/intersections in the path and removes the segments forming loops, optionally inserting the exact intersection points.

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{smooth()}{smooth()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Path}{Path}} hmap\+::smooth (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Path}{Path}} \&}]{path,  }\item[{int}]{navg = {\ttfamily 1},  }\item[{float}]{averaging\+\_\+intensity = {\ttfamily 1.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{float}]{inertia = {\ttfamily 0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Applies a smoothing operation to the path points using a moving average filter. 

This method smooths the path points based on a specified number of neighboring points, an averaging intensity, and an inertia factor. The smoothing involves calculating the average of neighboring points within a range defined by {\ttfamily navg}, and then applying an intensity-\/based weighted average to blend the original and smoothed values. Additionally, an inertia effect can be applied to gradually adjust point positions based on previous points.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em path} & The input path to be smoothed. \\
\hline
{\em navg} & Number of neighboring points to consider on each side of the current point during the smoothing process. Higher values result in broader smoothing. \\
\hline
{\em averaging\+\_\+intensity} & The weight given to the averaged points. A value of 1.\+0 applies full intensity, resulting in a complete averaging of the neighboring points. Lower values retain more of the original point\textquotesingle{}s position. \\
\hline
{\em inertia} & The factor by which each point is influenced by its previous point after the initial smoothing pass. A value of 0 has no inertia effect, while a higher value blends the current point\textquotesingle{}s position with that of the preceding point, creating a trailing effect.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Generates a continuous, non-\/self-\/intersecting squiggle curve by applying the squiggle recursive triangle subdivision algorithm to each edge of the input path. 

Implements the squiggle curve construction from Prusinkiewicz et al., "{}\+Generating Mountainous Terrain"{}. Constrained within domain triangles for each edge, ensuring continuity and absence of self-\/intersections.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em path} & The input path to apply the squiggle algorithm to. \\
\hline
{\em iterations} & Number of recursive subdivision levels per edge (e.\+g., 2 to 6). \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed number for deterministic edge selection. \\
\hline
{\em height\+\_\+ratio} & Height of the bounding triangle relative to edge length (default 0.\+5). \\
\hline
{\em orientation} & Displacement direction\+: 0 to alternate sides, 1 for positive normal, -\/1 for negative normal. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+weights} & Optional pointer to an \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} defining spatial weights to bias path progression. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional pointer to a binary/mask \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} (1 = allowed, 0 = forbidden) preventing the path from entering forbidden areas. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box for spatial sampling. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Generated continuous \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Path}{Path}.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Computes the 2D cross product of vectors formed by three points. 

Given three points p0, p1, and p2 in 2D space, this function computes the scalar cross product of the vectors (p1 -\/ p0) and (p2 -\/ p0). In 2D, the cross product is a scalar value and is often used to determine the orientation of the three points or the signed area of the parallelogram they form.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}

\hline

\hline
{\em p2} & The third point, forming the second vector p2 -\/ p0. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
The scalar value of the 2D cross product.
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Positive if the points p0, p1, p2 are oriented counterclockwise.
\item Negative if they are oriented clockwise.
\item Zero if the points are collinear. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyReturn}

Performs a Catmull-\/\+Rom spline interpolation. 

Interpolates a point on a Catmull-\/\+Rom spline defined by the points {\ttfamily p0}, {\ttfamily p1}, {\ttfamily p2}, and {\ttfamily p3}. The points {\ttfamily p1} and {\ttfamily p2} define the segment of the curve to be interpolated, while {\ttfamily p0} and {\ttfamily p3} are used as additional control points. The parameter {\ttfamily t} should be within the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}, where {\ttfamily t = 0} corresponds to the start point {\ttfamily p1} and {\ttfamily t = 1} corresponds to the end point {\ttfamily p2}.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em p0} & The first control point (influence for the start point). \\
\hline
{\em p1} & The second control point (start point of the segment). \\
\hline
{\em p2} & The third control point (end point of the segment). \\
\hline
{\em p3} & The fourth control point (influence for the end point). \\
\hline
{\em t} & The interpolation parameter, ranging from 0 to 1. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
The interpolated point on the Catmull-\/\+Rom spline.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Performs a De Casteljau algorithm-\/based interpolation for Bezier curves. 

Interpolates a point on a Bézier curve defined by a set of control points using De Casteljau\textquotesingle{}s algorithm. The algorithm is recursive and provides a stable and numerically robust method to evaluate Bézier curves at a given parameter {\ttfamily t}.

The parameter {\ttfamily t} should be within the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}, where {\ttfamily t = 0} corresponds to the first control point and {\ttfamily t = 1} corresponds to the last control point.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em points} & A vector of control points defining the Bézier curve. \\
\hline
{\em t} & The interpolation parameter, ranging from 0 to 1. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
The interpolated point on the Bézier curve.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Compute the divergence of a 2D gradient field. 

Given two scalar fields representing the horizontal and vertical derivatives of a height map\+:  \[
    p(x, y) = \frac{\partial h}{\partial x}, \qquad q(x, y) = \frac{\partial
h}{\partial y}
\] this function returns the divergence\+:  \[
    f(x, y) = \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}(x, y)
            + \frac{\partial q}{\partial y}(x, y)
\]

The divergence is a key term for solving the Poisson equation $\nabla^2 h = f$ when reconstructing a height field from gradients or from a normal map.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em dx} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} of horizontal derivatives ( $\partial h / \partial x$). Must have the same dimensions as {\ttfamily dy}. \\
\hline
{\em dy} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} of vertical derivatives ( $\partial h / \partial y$). Must have the same dimensions as {\ttfamily dx}.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} containing the divergence $f(x, y)$ for each pixel. The returned array has the same size as the inputs.
\end{DoxyReturn}
See unit tests\+: \doxylink{test__gradient_8cpp}{test\+\_\+gradient.\+cpp} \Hypertarget{namespacehmap_ab0755dccfcae2b02a211c091e33f79a9}\label{namespacehmap_ab0755dccfcae2b02a211c091e33f79a9}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::gradient\+\_\+angle\+\_\+circular\+\_\+smoothing (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{int}]{ir,  }\item[{bool}]{downward = {\ttfamily false} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Computes a smoothed gradient angle (aspect) field with circular unwrapping. 

This function computes the gradient angle (aspect) of the input scalar field and applies a circular smoothing to remove discontinuities caused by the ±π wrap of the arctangent. The angle field is smoothed by converting the angle to a unit vector representation on the circle, applying a local smoothing kernel, and converting it back to an angle. This results in a continuous aspect map that is ideal for visualization or further processing.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input scalar field (e.\+g., a heightmap). \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius of the local smoothing kernel applied to the angle vectors. \\
\hline
{\em downward} & If set to {\ttfamily true}, angles are adjusted to point in the downslope direction (useful for hydrology or flow simulations). If {\ttfamily false}, angles point in the upslope direction.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
An \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} containing the smoothed gradient angles in radians, in the range \mbox{[}-\/π, π\mbox{]}.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Regions with very low gradient magnitude may produce unstable angle values; these regions should typically be masked or treated separately.
\item This function is suited for preserving continuous angular fields when the direction (not the orientation) of the gradient matters.
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Converts a normal map to a heightmap using direct summation of gradients. 

This function computes a heightmap from a given normal map ({\ttfamily nmap}) by integrating gradients derived from the normal map in two passes. The result is the average of two independent integrations to reduce artifacts from directional bias.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em nmap} & A 3D tensor representing the normal map. It should have three channels (X, Y, Z) and a shape of (width, height, 3). The values are assumed to be in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
An {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} object representing the computed heightmap with the same spatial dimensions as the input normal map (width, height).
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The algorithm assumes the normal map values are normalized between 0 and 1.
\item Two heightmaps ({\ttfamily z1} and {\ttfamily z2}) are computed using different traversal orders, and the final result is their average to reduce directional bias.

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{solve\_poisson\_gauss\_seidel()}{solve\_poisson\_gauss\_seidel()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::solve\+\_\+poisson\+\_\+gauss\+\_\+seidel (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{rhs,  }\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{h,  }\item[{int}]{iterations = {\ttfamily 500},  }\item[{float}]{omega = {\ttfamily 1.0f} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Solve the Poisson equation ∇²h = rhs using Gauss–\+Seidel iteration. 

This function assumes Dirichlet boundary conditions (height = 0 at the edges). The algorithm updates interior points according to\+: \[ h(x, y) = (1
- \omega) h(x, y)
          + \omega \cdot 0.25 \big(
              h(x+1, y) + h(x-1, y)
            + h(x, y+1) + h(x, y-1)
            - rhs(x, y)
            \big)
\]


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em rhs} & Right-\/hand side (divergence of gradients). \\
\hline
{\em h} & Height field to update; initialized to 0 or an estimate. \\
\hline
{\em iterations} & Number of Gauss–\+Seidel iterations to run. \\
\hline
{\em omega} & Relaxation parameter (1 = standard Gauss–\+Seidel, 1 \texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} omega \texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} 2 = over-\/relaxation). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\Hypertarget{namespacehmap_a3f8dc201377b61428eba8daa4a03a65f}\label{namespacehmap_a3f8dc201377b61428eba8daa4a03a65f}

Label drainage basins using a priority-\/flood algorithm. 

Starting from boundary cells, this function floods a 2D scalar field inward using a height-\/ordered priority queue and assigns each cell to a basin. Each boundary cell initializes a unique basin.

Connectivity is 8-\/neighbor. Spill elevations between basins are detected but not yet recorded.

\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\end{DoxyReturn}

Computes the number of drainage paths for each cell based on the D8 flow direction model. 

This function calculates the number of neighboring cells that have flow directions pointing to the current cell according to the D8 model. The result is an array where each cell contains the count of its incoming flow directions.

\end{DoxyParams}

Identifies flow apex (source) cells using D8 flow routing. 

A flow apex is defined as a cell with zero inflow neighbors (no upstream contributors) in the D8 flow graph. These cells correspond to drainage sources, ridge heads, or local flow origins.

Estimate lake water depths on a terrain by filling depressions. 

This function identifies depressions in a terrain elevation model and simulates the flooding of these areas to produce a lake system. It uses a rough depression-\/filling algorithm to compute the water surface, then subtracts the original elevations to obtain the water depth at each cell.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input 2D array representing terrain elevations (height field). \\
\hline
{\em surface\+\_\+threshold} & The minimum number of pixels a component must have to be retained. Components smaller than this threshold will be removed. The default value is 0 (no filtering).\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A 2D array representing the water depth for each cell. Values are zero where no lake is present and positive where water accumulates in depressions.
\end{DoxyReturn}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::flow\+\_\+accumulation\+\_\+stochastic (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{z,  }\item[{int}]{n\+\_\+samples = {\ttfamily 1~$<$$<$~19},  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed = {\ttfamily 0},  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+source = {\ttfamily nullptr},  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p\+\_\+decay = {\ttfamily nullptr} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Computes flow accumulation using a stochastic (Monte-\/\+Carlo) transport estimator. 

Particles are spawned uniformly, advected along the downhill gradient field with exact voxel traversal, attenuated by an optional decay term, and deposit flux into every cell they exit. A final analytic normalization yields the steady-\/state flux, including for cells no particle visited. Compared to flow\+\_\+accumulation\+\_\+d8, the result is smooth and free of axis-\/aligned artifacts.

Port of the reference implementation of "{}\+Stochastic Geomorphological \+Transport for Terrain Erosion Simulation"{} (N. Mc\+Donald, G. Cordonnier), \href{https://github.com/erosiv/geotransport}{\texttt{ https\+://github.\+com/erosiv/geotransport}} (MIT).

Results are reproducible up to floating-\/point summation order (deposits accumulate via unordered atomic adds).


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input array representing the heightmap values. \\
\hline
{\em n\+\_\+samples} & Number of Monte-\/\+Carlo samples (particles). \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed number (deterministic for fixed inputs). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+source} & Optional per-\/cell source term (default\+: uniform 1). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+decay} & Optional per-\/cell decay rate (default\+: 0, pure accumulation). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Per-\/cell steady-\/state flux.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Computes the flow accumulation for each cell using the Multiple Flow Direction (MFD) model. 

This function calculates the flow accumulation for each cell based on the MFD model {\bfseries [Qin2007]}. Flow accumulation represents the total amount of flow that accumulates at each cell from upstream cells. The flow-\/partition exponent is locally defined using a reference talus value, where smaller values of {\ttfamily talus\+\_\+ref} will lead to narrower flow streams. The maximum talus value of the heightmap can be used as a reference.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input array representing the heightmap values. \\
\hline
{\em talus\+\_\+ref} & Reference talus used to locally define the flow-\/partition exponent. Small values will result in thinner flow streams. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} An array where each cell contains the computed flow accumulation.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Computes averaged D-\/infinity flow accumulation with terrain perturbations. 

This function estimates flow accumulation using the D∞ (D-\/infinity) method by perturbing the input elevation map multiple times with Perlin noise. For each sample, a noise field is added to the terrain, the flow accumulation is computed, and results are accumulated and averaged.

The perturbation introduces stochastic variability, which can help reduce numerical artifacts and improve robustness in flat or ambiguous flow regions.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input elevation array. \\
\hline
{\em talus\+\_\+ref} & Reference talus angle (or slope threshold) used by the D∞ algorithm. \\
\hline
{\em nsamples} & Number of noise-\/perturbed samples to average. \\
\hline
{\em kw} & Noise frequency scaling factor. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Base random seed (incremented for each sample). \\
\hline
{\em amp} & Amplitude of the noise perturbation. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box used for noise generation.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Averaged flow accumulation array.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Computes the flow direction and weights for each direction using the Multiple Flow Direction (MFD) model. 

This function calculates the flow direction for each cell and provides the weight for each possible flow direction using the MFD model {\bfseries [Qin2007]}. The flow-\/partition exponent is determined using a reference talus value. Smaller values of {\ttfamily talus\+\_\+ref} will lead to thinner flow streams. The maximum talus value of the heightmap can be used as a reference.

{\em z} & Input array representing the heightmap values. \\
\hline
{\em talus\+\_\+ref} & Reference talus used to locally define the flow-\/partition exponent. Smaller values will result in thinner flow streams. \\

Computes the optimal flow path from a starting point to the boundary of a given elevation array. 

This function finds the flow path on a grid represented by the input array {\ttfamily z}, starting from the given point {\ttfamily ij\+\_\+start}. It identifies the best path to the boundary, minimizing upward elevation penalties while accounting for distance and elevation factors.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & The input 2D array representing elevation values. \\
\hline
{\em ij\+\_\+start} & The starting point as a 2D vector of indices (i, j) within the array. \\
\hline
{\em elevation\+\_\+ratio} & Weight for elevation difference in the cost function (default\+: 0.\+5). \\
\hline
{\em distance\+\_\+exponent} & Exponent for the distance term in the cost function (default\+: 2.\+0). \\
\hline
{\em upward\+\_\+penalization} & Penalty factor for upward elevation changes (default\+: 100.\+0). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Path}{Path} object representing the optimal flow path with normalized x and y coordinates and corresponding elevations.
\end{DoxyReturn}
The output path consists of\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Normalized x-\/coordinates along the path.
\item Normalized y-\/coordinates along the path.
\item Elevation values corresponding to each point on the path.
\end{DoxyItemize}

Generates a 2D array representing a riverbed based on a specified path. 

This function calculates a scalar depth field ({\ttfamily dz}) for a riverbed shape using a path, which can optionally be smoothed with Bezier curves. It supports noise perturbation and post-\/filtering to adjust the riverbed\textquotesingle{}s features.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em path} & The input path defining the riverbed\textquotesingle{}s trajectory. \\
\hline
{\em shape} & The dimensions of the output array (width, height). \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & The bounding box for the output grid in world coordinates. \\
\hline
{\em bezier\+\_\+smoothing} & Flag to enable or disable Bezier smoothing of the path. \\
\hline
{\em depth\+\_\+start} & The depth at the start of the riverbed. \\
\hline
{\em depth\+\_\+end} & The depth at the end of the riverbed. \\
\hline
{\em slope\+\_\+start} & The slope multiplier at the start of the riverbed. \\
\hline
{\em slope\+\_\+end} & The slope multiplier at the end of the riverbed. \\
\hline
{\em shape\+\_\+exponent\+\_\+start} & The shape exponent at the start of the riverbed. \\
\hline
{\em shape\+\_\+exponent\+\_\+end} & The shape exponent at the end of the riverbed. \\
\hline
{\em k\+\_\+smoothing} & The smoothing factor for the riverbed shape adjustments. \\
\hline
{\em post\+\_\+filter\+\_\+ir} & The radius of the post-\/filtering operation for smoothing the output. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Optional pointer to a noise array for perturbing the x-\/coordinates. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Optional pointer to a noise array for perturbing the y-\/coordinates. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+r} & Optional pointer to a noise array for perturbing the radial function. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A 2D array representing the calculated riverbed depth field.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The function requires the path to have at least two points. If the path has fewer points, an empty array is returned with the given shape.
\end{DoxyNote}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::water\+\_\+depth\+\_\+from\+\_\+mask (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{z,  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{mask,  }\item[{float}]{mask\+\_\+threshold = {\ttfamily 0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{int}]{iterations\+\_\+max = {\ttfamily 10000},  }\item[{float}]{tolerance = {\ttfamily 1e-\/2\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Compute water depth over a masked terrain using harmonic interpolation. 

This function estimates the water depth above a terrain surface by solving a Laplace equation on the domain defined by {\ttfamily mask}. The solution is obtained using the harmonic interpolation method with Successive Over-\/\+Relaxation (SOR). The resulting water depth is given by the difference between the interpolated surface and the original terrain elevation.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Input 2D array representing the terrain elevations (height field). \\
\hline
{\em mask} & Mask array of the same shape as {\ttfamily z}. Values greater than {\ttfamily mask\+\_\+threshold} define regions where water can accumulate, while lower values represent boundaries or fixed terrain. \\
\hline
{\em mask\+\_\+threshold} & Threshold used to convert {\ttfamily mask} into a binary field (0 or 1) for identifying water/terrain boundaries. \\
\hline
{\em iterations\+\_\+max} & Maximum number of SOR iterations used in the harmonic interpolation. \\
\hline
{\em tolerance} & Convergence criterion\+: the algorithm stops if the maximum absolute update between iterations is less than this value.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A 2D array containing the computed water depth at each grid cell. Depth values are non-\/negative where water is present and zero where the mask indicates no water.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Apply a drying factor to a water depth field. 

This function reduces the water depth values in-\/place by multiplying them by a given {\ttfamily dry\+\_\+out\+\_\+ratio}. If a mask is provided, the drying is applied only where the mask is non-\/zero, allowing selective drying of specific regions.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em water\+\_\+depth} & Reference to the 2D array containing water depth values. The array is modified in-\/place. \\
\hline
{\em dry\+\_\+out\+\_\+ratio} & Multiplicative factor (typically between 0 and 1) used to scale down the water depth. A value of 1 leaves the depth unchanged, while 0 removes all water. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask} & Optional pointer to a mask array of the same shape as {\ttfamily water\+\_\+depth}. Drying is applied only where the mask has non-\/zero values. If {\ttfamily nullptr}, the factor is applied uniformly to all cells. \\
\hline
{\em depth\+\_\+max} & Maximum water depth, computed automatically by default.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{water\_depth\_increase()}{water\_depth\_increase()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::water\+\_\+depth\+\_\+increase (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{water\+\_\+depth,  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{z,  }\item[{float}]{additional\+\_\+depth }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Simulates a local increase in water depth without global reflooding. 

This function propagates an additional water depth over a terrain elevation map ({\ttfamily z}), starting only from cells that already contain water in the input {\ttfamily water\+\_\+depth} array. The propagation is restricted to neighboring cells of higher elevation (8-\/connectivity), preventing the formation of entirely new flooded basins disconnected from the original water region.

Unlike \doxylink{namespacehmap_afad09b723c82dd7f0a0f7365e74b1edf}{water\+\_\+depth\+\_\+increase\+\_\+with\+\_\+flooding()}, this function does not perform a full flooding simulation of the domain. It is primarily intended for expanding or softening an existing water mask slightly beyond the current shoreline.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em water\+\_\+depth} & Input array representing the initial water depth. \\
\hline
{\em z} & Elevation array corresponding to the same grid as {\ttfamily water\+\_\+depth}. \\
\hline
{\em additional\+\_\+depth} & Additional water depth to propagate from the existing water region. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
An \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} containing the updated water depth after local propagation.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
Water spreads only upward toward neighboring cells with higher elevation. Existing disconnected dry basins are not flooded.

This function is useful for generating extended shoreline masks, erosion influence regions, or visually expanding water boundaries without performing a physically complete flooding simulation.
\end{DoxyNote}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{water\_depth\_increase\_with\_flooding()}{water\_depth\_increase\_with\_flooding()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::water\+\_\+depth\+\_\+increase\+\_\+with\+\_\+flooding (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{water\+\_\+depth,  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{z,  }\item[{float}]{additional\+\_\+depth }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Simulates a physical rise in water level with full domain flooding. 

This function increases the water level by {\ttfamily additional\+\_\+depth} and recomputes flooding over the terrain elevation map ({\ttfamily z}). Unlike \doxylink{namespacehmap_a136f042ce2ad8c14033f4d839f56265d}{water\+\_\+depth\+\_\+increase()}, the propagation is not restricted to the vicinity of the original water region\+: water may spread through connected terrain and flood previously dry areas if they become reachable under the new water level.

The simulation behaves more like a physical flooding process where rising water can overflow barriers, connect basins, and eventually inundate large portions of the domain depending on terrain topology.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em water\+\_\+depth} & Input array representing the initial water depth. \\
\hline
{\em z} & Elevation array corresponding to the same grid as {\ttfamily water\+\_\+depth}. \\
\hline
{\em additional\+\_\+depth} & Additional water depth used to raise the global water level. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
An \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} containing the updated flooded state after recomputing water propagation.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
Flood propagation may extend far beyond the original water mask and can potentially inundate the entire connected terrain domain.

This function is more physically plausible than \doxylink{namespacehmap_a136f042ce2ad8c14033f4d839f56265d}{water\+\_\+depth\+\_\+increase()}, and is suitable for terrain flooding simulations, overflow analysis, or hydrological studies.
\end{DoxyNote}

Pads the beginning of a string with zeros until it reaches a specified length. 

This function prepends \textquotesingle{}0\textquotesingle{} characters to the input string {\ttfamily str} so that the resulting string has at least {\ttfamily n\+\_\+zero} characters. If {\ttfamily str} is already equal to or longer than {\ttfamily n\+\_\+zero}, it is returned unchanged.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em str} & The input string to pad. \\
\hline
{\em n\+\_\+zero} & The minimum total length of the resulting string after padding. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new string padded with leading zeros to reach the specified length.
\end{DoxyReturn}
{\bfseries{Example}} 
\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacehmap_a3f38b7faedc76835a0a902eb48e3d94b}{zfill}}(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}42"{}},\ 5);\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ returns\ "{}00042"{}}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacehmap_a3f38b7faedc76835a0a902eb48e3d94b}{zfill}}(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}12345"{}},\ 5);\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ returns\ "{}12345"{}}}

\end{DoxyCode}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::harmonic\+\_\+interpolation (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{mask\+\_\+fixed\+\_\+values,  }\item[{int}]{iterations\+\_\+max = {\ttfamily 500},  }\item[{float}]{tolerance = {\ttfamily 1e-\/5\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}},  }\item[{float}]{omega = {\ttfamily 0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Perform harmonic interpolation on a 2D array using the Successive Over-\/\+Relaxation (SOR) method. 

This function solves the discrete Laplace equation on a regular grid by iteratively updating the values of an input array. Values marked as fixed in the {\ttfamily mask\+\_\+fixed\+\_\+values} remain unchanged throughout the process. The algorithm stops when either the maximum number of iterations is reached or the change between successive iterations falls below the specified tolerance.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input 2D array providing the initial guess for the solution. \\
\hline
{\em mask\+\_\+fixed\+\_\+values} & Mask of the same shape as {\ttfamily array}. Cells with a value greater than zero indicate fixed points that must remain unchanged during interpolation. \\
\hline
{\em iterations\+\_\+max} & Maximum number of SOR iterations to perform. \\
\hline
{\em tolerance} & Convergence criterion\+: the algorithm stops if the maximum absolute update between iterations is less than this value. \\
\hline
{\em omega} & Relaxation factor (1 \texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} omega \texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} 2 recommended). Values closer to 2 accelerate convergence, but overly large values may cause divergence.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new 2D array containing the interpolated solution.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The algorithm updates only the interior points (indices {\ttfamily \mbox{[}1..nx-\/2, 1..ny-\/2\mbox{]}}).
\item Cells where {\ttfamily mask\+\_\+fixed\+\_\+values(i, j) \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 0} remain unchanged.
\item A relaxation factor of 1 corresponds to the standard Jacobi/\+Gauss-\/\+Seidel update. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Perform harmonic interpolation on a 2D array with 2D variable diffusion coefficients (Dx, Dy) using the Successive Over-\/\+Relaxation (SOR) method. 

Solves the steady-\/state anisotropic diffusion equation\+:  \[
\nabla \cdot (\mathbf{D} \nabla u) = \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(D_x
\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\right) +
\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(D_y \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right) = 0
\]


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input 2D array providing the initial guess. \\
\hline
{\em mask\+\_\+fixed\+\_\+values} & Mask where values \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 0 indicate fixed boundary constraints. \\
\hline
{\em dx} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} of diffusion coefficients in the x-\/direction. \\
\hline
{\em dy} & \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} of diffusion coefficients in the y-\/direction. \\
\hline
{\em iterations\+\_\+max} & Maximum number of SOR iterations. \\
\hline
{\em tolerance} & Convergence tolerance. \\
\hline
{\em omega} & Relaxation factor (0 = auto-\/computed optimal). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Interpolated array. 
\end{DoxyReturn}

Generates a biweight kernel array. 

This function creates a biweight kernel, which is a type of kernel function used in statistics for smoothing and interpolation.

For each cell, follows the steepest-\/descending flow path and returns the number of downstream cells required to leave the domain. Cells whose flow terminates in an internal sink have a path length of 0.

Computes the local median deviation of a 2D array. 

This function calculates the absolute difference between the local mean and a pseudo-\/local median of each element in the input array. The local neighborhood is defined by a square window with radius {\ttfamily ir}.

\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new array of the same size as {\ttfamily array}, where each element represents the absolute deviation between the local mean and pseudo-\/local median in its neighborhood.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The function uses a pseudo-\/median approximation. For exact median computation, replace the {\ttfamily \doxylink{namespacehmap_a14eb6b7d304484c8cbb231b672851491}{median\+\_\+pseudo()}} call with a proper median filter implementation.

Return the local mean based on a mean filter with a square kernel. 

This function calculates the local mean of the input array using a mean filter with a square kernel. The local mean is determined by averaging values within a square neighborhood defined by the footprint radius {\ttfamily ir}. The result is an array where each value represents the mean of the surrounding values within the kernel size.

Generates a function representing an erosion profile based on the specified type and parameters. 

This function returns a callable object ({\ttfamily std\+::function}) that computes the value of the specified erosion profile for a given phase angle (phi). Optionally, it can compute the average value of the profile over the range \mbox{[}-\/π, π\mbox{]}.

\hline
{\em delta} & A parameter that can influence the profile (depending on the profile choice). \\
\hline

\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A {\ttfamily std\+::function\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<}float(float)\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}} that computes the erosion profile for a given phase angle.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\begin{DoxyExceptions}{Exceptions}
{\em std\+::invalid\+\_\+argument} & \\
\hline
\end{DoxyExceptions}
{\ttfamily erosion\+\_\+profile} is invalid.

\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The average value is computed using numerical integration over 50 sample points within \mbox{[}-\/π, π\mbox{]}. 
\end{DoxyNote}

{\em phasor\+\_\+profile} & The type of phasor profile to generate. \\
\hline
{\em delta} & A parameter that can influence the profile (depending on the profile choice). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+profile\+\_\+avg} & Optional pointer to a float. If not {\ttfamily nullptr}, it will store the average value of the profile over the range \mbox{[}-\/π, π\mbox{]}. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A {\ttfamily std\+::function\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<}float(float)\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}} that computes the phasor profile for a given phase angle.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Returns a normalized radial profile function. 

The returned function maps x ∈ \mbox{[}0,1\mbox{]} to a value in \mbox{[}0,1\mbox{]}, with f(0) = 0 and f(1) = 1. It is typically used for radial or distance-\/based falloff in procedural heightmaps.

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{closing\_by\_reconstruction()}{closing\_by\_reconstruction()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::closing\+\_\+by\+\_\+reconstruction (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{int}]{ir,  }\item[{float}]{k\+\_\+smooth\+\_\+max = {\ttfamily 0.\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Apply closing by reconstruction to the input array. 

Performs a dilation followed by a reconstruction by erosion, filling small dark regions while preserving the shape of larger structures.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius of the structuring element. \\
\hline
{\em k\+\_\+smooth\+\_\+max} & Smoothness factor (0 for hard max). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Result after closing by reconstruction. 
\end{DoxyReturn}

Smooth contour boundaries of segmented regions. 

Reduces staircase artifacts on component borders by smoothing the transition zone around edges.

\hline
{\em ir} & Radius of the smoothing kernel. \\
\hline
{\em transition\+\_\+ratio} & Controls edge blending width. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} with smoothed contours.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{dilation\_expand\_border\_only()}{dilation\_expand\_border\_only()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::dilation\+\_\+expand\+\_\+border\+\_\+only (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{int}]{ir }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Expand non-\/zero regions of an array by morphological dilation, while preserving the original non-\/zero values. 

This function performs a local-\/maximum (dilation) operation on the input array with a given radius {\ttfamily ir}, then copies back the original non-\/zero values so they remain unchanged. Only the surrounding background is filled with expanded values, effectively “growing” the borders of non-\/zero regions.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input 2D array where non-\/zero cells represent regions of interest and zero cells represent background. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius of the dilation (in grid cells). Defines how far the non-\/zero values can expand into the background.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new 2D array where the borders of non-\/zero regions have been expanded outward by up to {\ttfamily ir} cells, while the original non-\/zero values are kept intact. 
\end{DoxyReturn}

Return the Euclidean distance transform. 

Exact transform based on Meijster et al. algorithm {\bfseries [Meijster2000]}.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array to be transformed, will be converted into binary\+: 1 wherever input is greater than 0, 0 elsewhere. \\
\hline
{\em return\+\_\+squared\+\_\+distance} & Whether the distance returned is squared or not. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Reference to the output array.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\index{hmap@{hmap}!morphological\_laplacian@{morphological\_laplacian}}
\index{morphological\_laplacian@{morphological\_laplacian}!hmap@{hmap}}
\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{morphological\_laplacian()}{morphological\_laplacian()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::morphological\+\_\+laplacian (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{int}]{ir }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Apply a morphological Laplacian operator to the input array using a square structure. 

Compared to the classical Laplacian, this operator is more robust to noise and better preserves sharp features, as it relies on morphological extrema rather than linear differences.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array to which the morphological Laplacian is applied. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius of the square kernel used for the underlying dilation and erosion operations. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Output array containing the morphological Laplacian.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Apply opening by reconstruction to the input array. 

Performs an erosion followed by a reconstruction by dilation, removing small bright features while preserving the shape of larger structures.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input array. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Radius of the structuring element. \\
\hline
{\em k\+\_\+smooth\+\_\+min} & Smoothness factor (0 for hard min). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Result after opening by reconstruction. 
\end{DoxyReturn}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{relative\_distance\_from\_skeleton()}{relative\_distance\_from\_skeleton()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::relative\+\_\+distance\+\_\+from\+\_\+skeleton (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{int}]{ir\+\_\+search,  }\item[{bool}]{zero\+\_\+at\+\_\+borders = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{int}]{ir\+\_\+erosion = {\ttfamily 1} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Computes the relative distance of each non-\/zero cell in a binary array from the skeleton and border. 

This function calculates a relative distance measure for each non-\/zero cell in the input array. The measure is defined as the ratio of the cell\textquotesingle{}s distance to the nearest border and the combined distances to the nearest skeleton and border cells. The skeleton is computed using the Zhang-\/\+Suen skeletonization algorithm.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The input binary array for which the relative distance map is to be calculated. Non-\/zero values are considered for processing. \\
\hline
{\em ir\+\_\+search} & The search radius for finding the nearest skeleton and border cells. \\
\hline
{\em zero\+\_\+at\+\_\+borders} & If true, the borders of the skeletonized image will be set to zero. \\
\hline
{\em ir\+\_\+erosion} & The erosion radius applied to the skeleton. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
An array representing the relative distance map, where each cell has a value between 0 and 1. A value closer to 1 indicates proximity to the skeleton, while a value closer to 0 indicates proximity to the border.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The skeleton is computed using the Zhang-\/\+Suen skeletonization algorithm.
\end{DoxyNote}

Positive values indicate convex regions, negative values concave regions.

\end{DoxyReturn}

Computes a signed distance transform using curvature sign. 

First computes the unsigned Euclidean distance transform, then assigns its sign from the curvature of the smoothed distance field\+: sign = sign( div( ∇d / \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}∇d\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} ) ).


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}

\hline

\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Signed distance transform.

Computes the skeleton of a binary image using the Zhang-\/\+Suen skeletonization algorithm. 

This function processes a binary input array to extract its skeleton by iteratively thinning the image until no further changes occur. It optionally sets the borders of the resulting skeletonized image to zero.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The input binary array to be skeletonized. Values should typically be 0 or 1. \\
\hline
{\em zero\+\_\+at\+\_\+borders} & If true, the borders of the resulting array will be set to zero. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
The skeletonized version of the input array.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
This implementation is based on the algorithm described at \href{https://github.com/krishraghuram/Zhang-Suen-Skeletonization}{\texttt{ https\+://github.\+com/krishraghuram/\+Zhang-\/\+Suen-\/\+Skeletonization}}.
\end{DoxyNote}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::downscale\+\_\+transform (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{float}]{kc,  }\item[{std\+::function$<$ void(\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&x)$>$}]{unary\+\_\+op,  }\item[{bool}]{apply\+\_\+prefiltering = {\ttfamily false} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Applies a downscaling transformation to a 2D array using Fourier-\/based filtering. 

This function performs a series of operations on a 2D array to isolate and transform its low-\/frequency components. It uses a Fourier transform for filtering, downscales the array for efficient processing, applies a user-\/defined unary operation, and then restores the transformed low-\/frequency content to the original resolution.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & A reference to the input 2D array to be transformed. The array may be resized internally. \\
\hline
{\em kc} & The cutoff wavenumber for isolating low-\/frequency components during filtering. \\
\hline
{\em unary\+\_\+op} & A user-\/defined function that applies a transformation to the downscaled array.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The function ensures that the input array is square for Fourier operations by resampling it if necessary.
\item A smooth low-\/pass filter is applied in the frequency domain, and the filtered array is downscaled to a coarse resolution.
\item The user-\/defined transformation ({\ttfamily unary\+\_\+op}) is applied to the downscaled array.
\item The transformed low-\/frequency content is upsampled and reintegrated into the original array.
\item If the input array was not square, the final result is resampled back to its original shape.
