{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::upscale\+\_\+amplification (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{int}]{upscaling\+\_\+levels,  }\item[{float}]{persistence,  }\item[{std\+::function$<$ void(\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&x, float current\+\_\+scaling)$>$}]{unary\+\_\+op }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Applies an upscaling amplification process to an array, followed by a unary operation. 

This function progressively upscales the given array by powers of 2 (starting from the initial shape), performs a user-\/defined unary operation on the upscaled array at each level, and finally returns the array to its original resolution using bilinear interpolation.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & A reference to the array that will be upscaled and processed. \\
\hline
{\em upscaling\+\_\+levels} & The number of upscaling levels to apply. The function will resample the array for each level. \\
\hline
{\em persistence} & A scaling factor applied at each level to adjust the impact of the unary operation. Higher persistence values will amplify the effects at each level. \\
\hline
{\em unary\+\_\+op} & A user-\/defined unary operation to apply to the array at each upscaling level. The operation takes a reference to the array.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The function first applies bicubic resampling to upscale the array, then applies the user-\/provided {\ttfamily unary\+\_\+op} at each upscaling level. After all levels are processed, the array is resampled back to its initial shape using bilinear interpolation. 
\end{DoxyNote}

Adds a smoothed maximum value from a kernel to a specified position in a 2D array. 

This function applies a truncated kernel to the given array at position (ic, jc), where the kernel is truncated to ensure it fits within the array\textquotesingle{}s bounds. The maximum value between the current array value and the kernel value is computed using a smoothing factor, and the result is stored back in the array.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Reference to the 2D array (heightmap) where the kernel is applied. \\
\hline
{\em kernel} & The kernel array containing values to be applied to the array. \\
\hline
{\em k\+\_\+smooth} & The smoothing factor used in the maximum\+\_\+smooth function. \\
\hline
{\em ic} & The x-\/coordinate of the center in the array where the kernel is applied. \\
\hline
{\em jc} & The y-\/coordinate of the center in the array where the kernel is applied.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
The kernel is truncated to ensure it fits within the bounds of the array. After applying the kernel, the values in the array are updated with the result of the maximum\+\_\+smooth function. \Hypertarget{namespacehmap_acafd15472972fb139c59071c091741cf}\label{namespacehmap_acafd15472972fb139c59071c091741cf}

Rescales the values of a vector to a specified range. 

This function linearly rescales all elements in {\ttfamily vec} so that their new values lie within the range \mbox{[}{\ttfamily vmin}, {\ttfamily vmax}\mbox{]}. The rescaling is based on the current minimum and maximum values found in the input vector.

Special cases\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item If {\ttfamily vec} is empty, the function does nothing.
\item If {\ttfamily vmin == vmax}, all elements are set to {\ttfamily vmax}.
\item If all elements of {\ttfamily vec} are equal, they are replaced by that constant value.

Generates a diffusion-\/limited aggregation (DLA) pattern. 

This function simulates the diffusion-\/limited aggregation process to generate a pattern within a grid of specified dimensions. The DLA process models particles that undergo a random walk until they stick to a seed, gradually forming complex fractal structures.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & The dimensions of the grid where the DLA pattern will be generated. It is represented as a {\ttfamily glm\+::ivec2} object, where the first element is the width and the second element is the height. \\
\hline
{\em scale} & A scaling factor that influences the density of the particles in the DLA pattern. \\
\hline
{\em seeding\+\_\+radius} & The radius within which initial seeding of particles occurs. This radius defines the area where the first particles are placed. \\
\hline
{\em seeding\+\_\+outer\+\_\+radius\+\_\+ratio} & The ratio between the outer seeding radius and the initial seeding radius. It determines the outer boundary for particle seeding. \\
\hline
{\em slope} & Slope of the talus added to the DLA pattern. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+ratio} & A parameter that controls the amount of randomness or noise introduced in the talus formation process. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & The seed for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the pattern. The same seed will generate the same pattern.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A 2D array representing the generated DLA pattern. The array is of the same size as specified by {\ttfamily shape}.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\begin{DoxyCodeInclude}{0}

Generate a bounded band (capsule) mask. 

Creates a 0 to 1 mask shaped as a capsule\+: the value is 1 on a core segment defined by {\ttfamily center}, {\ttfamily angle} and {\ttfamily length}, and falls off to 0 at a distance {\ttfamily width} from the segment, following the requested radial profile. Typical uses\+: mountain-\/range envelopes, island-\/chain arc envelopes and, with a length larger than the domain, latitude bands / polar caps (place {\ttfamily center} on or beyond a domain edge).


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Output array shape. \\
\hline
{\em angle} & Band orientation angle in degrees. \\
\hline
{\em length} & Core segment length in normalized domain units. A zero length degenerates to a radial bump. \\
\hline
{\em width} & Falloff half-\/width in normalized domain units. \\
\hline
{\em profile} & Radial profile used for the falloff. \\
\hline
{\em profile\+\_\+param} & Additional parameter for the profile. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+r} & Optional noise array used to locally perturb the falloff distance (edge displacement). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+offset} & Optional noise array used to locally offset the band axis position (normalized by {\ttfamily width}). \\
\hline
{\em center} & Band center in normalized coordinates. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Domain bounding box. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Generated band mask in \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Generates a 2D Lorentzian bump pattern. 

This function fills an array with values computed from a normalized Lorentzian-\/shaped bump function. The bump is centered at a given position, has a specified radius, and can vary in width depending on a control parameter. Optional noise arrays can be applied to perturb the x and y coordinates before evaluation.

The Lorentzian function is normalized so that it returns 1.\+0 at the center and smoothly decays to 0.\+0 at the radius boundary. Outside the radius, the value is exactly 0.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Dimensions of the output array (width, height). \\
\hline
{\em width\+\_\+factor} & Scaling factor controlling the bump width relative to the control parameter. \\
\hline
{\em radius} & Radius of the bump in the coordinate space of {\ttfamily bbox}. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+ctrl\+\_\+param} & Optional pointer to an array of per-\/pixel control parameters. If provided, it modulates the width of the Lorentzian bump. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Optional pointer to an array of x-\/offset noise values. Values are added to the x coordinate before evaluation. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Optional pointer to an array of y-\/offset noise values. Values are added to the y coordinate before evaluation. \\
\hline
{\em center} & Center of the bump in the coordinate space of {\ttfamily bbox}. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) defining the coordinate space for the array.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} object of size {\ttfamily shape} containing the bump pattern.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The function normalizes the Lorentzian curve so that the maximum value is 1 at the center and smoothly decays to 0 at the boundary defined by {\ttfamily radius}.
\end{DoxyNote}

Generates a synthetic conical mountain heightmap. 

This function creates a simple cone-\/shaped elevation field centered at a given position. The cone profile follows a linear slope until it reaches the talus angle, resembling volcanic cones or alluvial fans. Optional displacement noise fields can be applied to perturb the cone shape.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Output array shape (resolution in x and y). \\
\hline

Generates a complex conical heightfield with valleys, directional bias, and radial waviness. 

This function procedurally constructs an island-\/like cone shape inside a 2D array. The height at each position is determined from the normalized radial distance to the center, with optional modulation by valleys, directional bias, and radial waviness. An erosion profile is applied to shape the valleys, and an optional control map can modulate the valley amplitude locally. The resulting height values are clamped to \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Output array dimensions (width, height). \\
\hline
{\em alpha} & Exponent controlling the steepness of the cone slope. \\
\hline
{\em radius} & Effective radius of the island (in coordinate space units). \\
\hline
{\em valley\+\_\+amp} & Global amplitude of valley depressions. \\
\hline
{\em valley\+\_\+nb} & Number of valleys around the island. \\
\hline
{\em valley\+\_\+decay\+\_\+ratio} & Controls how valley amplitude decays toward the center. \\
\hline
{\em valley\+\_\+angle0} & Angular offset of the first valley (in degrees). \\
\hline
{\em erosion\+\_\+profile} & Erosion profile type used for shaping valley cross-\/sections. \\
\hline
{\em erosion\+\_\+delta} & Smoothing parameter for the erosion profile function. \\
\hline
{\em radial\+\_\+waviness\+\_\+amp} & Amplitude of radial sinusoidal perturbations (coastal waviness). \\
\hline
{\em radial\+\_\+waviness\+\_\+kw} & Frequency multiplier for radial waviness. \\
\hline
{\em bias\+\_\+angle} & Direction (in degrees) of the slope bias (e.\+g. wind or sun exposure). \\
\hline
{\em bias\+\_\+amp} & Amplitude of the directional bias effect. \\
\hline
{\em bias\+\_\+exponent} & Controls how bias strength varies with radius. \\
\hline
{\em center} & Center position of the cone in coordinate space. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+ctrl\+\_\+param} & Optional control array; its values modulate the local valley amplitude. If nullptr, the valley amplitude is uniform. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Optional X-\/displacement noise field for coordinate perturbation. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Optional Y-\/displacement noise field for coordinate perturbation. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box defining the world coordinates covered by the array.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A 2D \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} containing the generated heightfield values in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Generates a smooth conical heightmap using a sigmoid-\/based profile. 

This function creates a 2D array representing a cone shape centered at a given position. The height decreases radially from the apex according to a sigmoid-\/shaped falloff, producing a smooth, rounded cone rather than a sharp linear one. Optionally, displacement noise can be applied along the X and Y axes to perturb the cone surface.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Dimensions of the output array (width, height). \\
\hline
{\em alpha} & Peak elevation value of the cone (controls maximum height). \\
\hline
{\em radius} & Radius of the cone base, expressed in normalized \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]} units relative to the bounding box. \\
\hline
{\em center} & Normalized coordinates of the cone’s center (default = \{0.\+5, 0.\+5\}). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Optional pointer to an array representing horizontal displacement noise (nullptr for none). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Optional pointer to an array representing vertical displacement noise (nullptr for none). \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box of the generated region in (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) order.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Generate a multi-\/step height profile along a rotated axis. 

Constructs an \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} where values follow a sequence of geometric steps blended with an optional linear transition. Steps are rotated by the given angle, can be shaped with an exponent, and may be modulated by optional control and noise fields.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Output array resolution. \\
\hline
{\em angle} & Rotation angle in degrees. \\
\hline
{\em r} & Geometric ratio between successive step widths. \\
\hline
{\em nsteps} & Number of steps. \\
\hline
{\em elevation\+\_\+exponent} & Exponent shaping step heights. \\
\hline
{\em shape\+\_\+gain} & Gain used to reshape intra-\/step transitions. \\
\hline
{\em scale} & Scale of the step axis. \\
\hline
{\em outer\+\_\+slope} & Slope outside the \mbox{[}0,1\mbox{]} axis interval. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+ctrl\+\_\+param} & Optional control parameter array. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Optional x-\/axis noise array. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Optional y-\/axis noise array. \\
\hline
{\em center} & Center of the step axis. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box of the domain. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Generated \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}.

Generates a rectangle-\/shaped heightmap with optional modifications. 

This function creates a 2D array representing a rectangle with specified dimensions, rotation, and optional parameters for customization such as control parameters, noise, and stretching.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Dimensions of the output array (width, height). \\
\hline
{\em rx} & Half-\/width of the rectangle, in normalized coordinates (0.\+0 to 1.\+0). \\
\hline
{\em ry} & Half-\/height of the rectangle, in normalized coordinates (0.\+0 to 1.\+0). \\
\hline
{\em angle} & Rotation angle of the rectangle in radians. Positive values rotate counterclockwise. \\
\hline
{\em slope} & Slope of the rectangle edge transition. A larger value makes the edge transition sharper. Defaults to 1.\+0. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+ctrl\+\_\+param} & Optional pointer to an {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} controlling custom parameters for the rectangle generation. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Optional pointer to an {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} for adding noise in the x-\/direction. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Optional pointer to an {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} for adding noise in the y-\/direction. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+stretching} & Optional pointer to an {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} for stretching the rectangle horizontally or vertically. \\
\hline
{\em center} & Center of the rectangle in normalized coordinates (0.\+0 to 1.\+0). Defaults to \{0.\+5, 0.\+5\}. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box for the rectangle in normalized coordinates \{x\+\_\+min, x\+\_\+max, y\+\_\+min, y\+\_\+max\}. Defaults to \{0.\+0, 1.\+0, 0.\+0, 1.\+0\}.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A 2D array representing the generated rectangle shape.

Generate a procedural impact crater heightmap. 

Creates a crater-\/shaped terrain with configurable inner cavity, outer lip, asymmetry, terraces, and optional central peak. Optional masks for the crater region and inner crater region can also be generated.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Output array shape. \\
\hline
{\em radius} & Crater radius. \\
\hline
{\em center} & Crater center position. \\
\hline
{\em angle} & Main asymmetry orientation angle in degrees. \\
\hline
{\em inner\+\_\+depth} & Depth of the crater cavity. \\
\hline
{\em inner\+\_\+exp} & Exponent controlling the inner profile shape. \\
\hline
{\em lip\+\_\+height} & Height of the crater rim. \\
\hline
{\em lip\+\_\+extent} & Extent of the outer rim. \\
\hline
{\em lip\+\_\+exp} & Exponent controlling rim falloff. \\
\hline
{\em asym\+\_\+ratio} & Asymmetry factor applied along the main direction. \\
\hline
{\em central\+\_\+peak\+\_\+height} & Height of the central peak. \\
\hline
{\em central\+\_\+peak\+\_\+extent} & Radius of the central peak region. \\
\hline
{\em n\+\_\+terraces} & Number of inner terraces. \\
\hline
{\em terrace\+\_\+extent} & Terrace spacing factor. \\
\hline
{\em terrace\+\_\+exp} & Terrace profile exponent. \\
\hline
{\em terrace\+\_\+persistence} & Terrace amplitude decay factor. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+r} & Optional radial noise distortion. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box coordinates. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+crater\+\_\+mask} & Optional output crater mask. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+inner\+\_\+crater\+\_\+mask} & Optional output inner crater mask. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Generated crater heightmap.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Generates a 2D island mask by perturbing a radial boundary with noise. 

Creates a binary mask of a single connected island using radial distance from a center point and adding an FBM-\/based angular displacement.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Output array size (width, height). \\
\hline
{\em radius} & Base island radius. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Noise seed. \\
\hline
{\em displacement} & Amplitude of boundary perturbation. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+type} & Type of underlying noise function. \\
\hline
{\em kw} & Angular frequency for sampling the noise. \\
\hline
{\em octaves} & Number of FBM octaves. \\
\hline
{\em weight} & Base amplitude of the FBM. \\
\hline
{\em persistence} & Amplitude falloff per octave. \\
\hline
{\em lacunarity} & Frequency multiplier per octave. \\
\hline
{\em center} & Center of the island in normalized coordinates. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Bounding box for coordinate remapping.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Binary mask where 1.\+f indicates land and 0.\+f indicates water.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Generates a land mask of an island chain scattered along a path. 

Spawns {\ttfamily island\+\_\+count} islands along the input path. Each island is an fbm-\/perturbed radial blob (same construction as {\ttfamily island\+\_\+land\+\_\+mask}). Island positions follow the path arc length, optionally jittered along and across the path by {\ttfamily scatter}. Island sizes follow a signed falloff\+: {\ttfamily size\+\_\+falloff = 0} gives uniform sizes, {\ttfamily +1} shrinks the islands toward the path end (hotspot-\/chain look, largest island at the head), {\ttfamily -\/1} shrinks them toward the start; {\ttfamily size\+\_\+jitter} adds per-\/island random variation.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Output array shape. \\
\hline
{\em path} & Input path (at least two points), in normalized domain coordinates. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed number. \\
\hline
{\em island\+\_\+count} & Number of islands spawned along the path. \\
\hline
{\em island\+\_\+radius} & Base island radius in normalized domain units. \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+falloff} & Signed size falloff along the path, in \mbox{[}-\/1, 1\mbox{]}. \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+jitter} & Per-\/island random radius variation ratio. \\
\hline
{\em scatter} & Random island displacement along and across the path. \\
\hline
{\em displacement} & Amplitude of the fbm boundary perturbation. \\
\hline
{\em noise\+\_\+type} & Noise type used for the boundary perturbation. \\
\hline
{\em kw} & Noise wavenumber. \\
\hline
{\em octaves} & Number of fbm octaves. \\
\hline
{\em weight} & Octave weighting. \\
\hline
{\em persistence} & Octave persistence. \\
\hline
{\em lacunarity} & Defines the wavenumber ratio between octaves. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Domain bounding box. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Binary land mask (0 or 1).
\end{DoxyReturn}

Generate a rift-\/shaped primitive. 

Creates a longitudinal depression centered around a rotated axis. The rift shape is defined by an outer radial profile, an optional bottom profile, and configurable inner/outer slopes. Noise fields can be used to locally perturb the radius and axial offset of the structure.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em shape} & Output array shape. \\
\hline
{\em angle} & Rift orientation angle in degrees. \\
\hline
{\em radius} & Rift half-\/width in normalized domain units. \\
\hline
{\em axial\+\_\+slope} & Longitudinal slope applied along the rift axis. \\
\hline
{\em depth} & Rift depth amplitude. \\
\hline
{\em scale\+\_\+with\+\_\+depth} & If true, scale radial features proportionally to the depth value. \\
\hline
{\em profile} & Radial profile used for the outer rift shape. \\
\hline
{\em profile\+\_\+param} & Additional parameter for the outer profile. \\
\hline
{\em bottom\+\_\+extent} & Relative extent of the flat or inner bottom region inside the rift. \\
\hline
{\em bottom\+\_\+depth} & Additional depth contribution applied to the bottom region. \\
\hline
{\em bottom\+\_\+profile} & Radial profile used for the bottom region. \\
\hline
{\em bottom\+\_\+profile\+\_\+param} & Additional parameter for the bottom profile. \\
\hline
{\em outer\+\_\+slope} & Slope factor controlling the outer falloff. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+r} & Optional noise array used to locally modulate the rift radius. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+offset} & Optional noise array used to locally offset the rift axis position. \\
\hline
{\em center} & Rift center in normalized coordinates. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Domain bounding box. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Generated rift array.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Clamps the values of an array according to the specified mode. 

This function modifies the input array in place based on one of three clamping modes\+:


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\bfseries{\doxylink{namespacehmap_ad4876bd26d1f3b33a1492645bfe50fbea7ee5673a01d4215ae4ba9ba95268ed59}{Clamp\+Mode\+::\+POSITIVE\+\_\+\+ONLY}}} Keeps only positive values and clamps them to a maximum value {\ttfamily vmax}. All negative values are set to 0.
\item {\bfseries{\doxylink{namespacehmap_ad4876bd26d1f3b33a1492645bfe50fbea10478d523fc507b9738e9cfdd5b7539c}{Clamp\+Mode\+::\+NEGATIVE\+\_\+\+ONLY}}} Keeps only negative values, reverses their sign (making them positive), and clamps them to a maximum value {\ttfamily vmax}. Positive values are set to 0.
\item {\bfseries{\doxylink{namespacehmap_ad4876bd26d1f3b33a1492645bfe50fbead7d8162264f038302952e47ad5e7a2ed}{Clamp\+Mode\+::\+BOTH}}} Keeps both positive and negative values, clamping them symmetrically between {\ttfamily -\/vmax} and {\ttfamily vmax}.
\end{DoxyItemize}


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Reference to the array whose values will be clamped. \\
\hline
{\em vmax} & The maximum absolute value used for clamping. \\
\hline
{\em mode} & The clamping mode to apply (see \doxylink{namespacehmap_ad4876bd26d1f3b33a1492645bfe50fbe}{Clamp\+Mode}). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Return the polynomial cubic smooth element-\/wise maximum of two arrays. 

This function computes the element-\/wise maximum of two input arrays with a smooth transition to avoid discontinuities that are present in the standard {\ttfamily maximum} function. The smoothness is controlled by the parameter {\ttfamily k}, which determines how smoothly the transition between the two arrays occurs.

The smooth transition is achieved using a polynomial cubic function, which provides a smooth blend between the two arrays. This approach helps in avoiding abrupt changes and can be useful in applications requiring smooth transitions.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array1} & First array to be compared. \\
\hline
{\em array2} & Second array to be compared. \\
\hline
{\em k} & Smoothing parameter in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. Higher values result in smoother transitions between the arrays (default is 0.\+2). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Element-\/wise smooth maximum between the two input arrays.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Return the polynomial cubic smooth maximum of two scalar values. 

This function computes the smooth maximum of two scalar values with a polynomial cubic smooth transition. The parameter {\ttfamily k} controls the degree of smoothness applied to the maximum calculation, ensuring a continuous and smooth blend between the two values.

The smooth transition helps in avoiding abrupt changes, making this function suitable for applications that require smooth variations.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em a} & First scalar value. \\
\hline
{\em b} & Second scalar value. \\
\hline
{\em k} & Smoothing parameter in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}. Higher values result in smoother transitions between the values (default is 0.\+2). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
float Smooth maximum value between the two input values.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Computes the signed distance field (SDF) of a 2D polyline. 

This function calculates the distance of each grid cell in the specified 2D array to the closest segment of a polyline. The polyline is represented by a {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Path}{Path}} object, and optional noise fields can be added to perturb the array coordinates.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em path} & The polyline path represented as a {\ttfamily \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Path}{Path}} object containing the nodes. \\
\hline
{\em shape} & The dimensions (width, height) of the output array grid. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & The bounding box of the array grid in the format (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Pointer to an optional noise array for perturbing x-\/coordinates (can be nullptr). \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Pointer to an optional noise array for perturbing y-\/coordinates (can be nullptr).\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} The resulting signed distance field (SDF) as a 2D array.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Perturb the contour of a binary mask using a displacement field, while trying to preserve a single connected component without holes. 

This function takes a binary mask and a noise map of the same size, computes the boundary of the mask, estimates a local outward normal for each boundary pixel, and displaces that pixel by an amount proportional to the noise value. The displacement is clamped to remain inside the image domain.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em mask} & Input binary mask as an \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} (0 = background, \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}0 = foreground). Must be at least 3×3 in size. \\
\hline
{\em noise} & Noise field providing signed displacement factors, typically in \mbox{[}-\/1, 1\mbox{]}. Must have the same dimensions as {\ttfamily mask}. \\
\hline
{\em max\+\_\+displacement} & Maximum displacement magnitude in pixels applied along the estimated boundary normal for each pixel. \\
\hline
{\em ir} & Neighborhood radius used for normal estimation and contour reconnection.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new \doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} representing the perturbed binary mask, with values 0 (background) and 1 (foreground), guaranteed to be a single connectedcomponent without holes.
\end{DoxyReturn}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily void hmap\+::select\+\_\+multiband3 (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{band\+\_\+low,  }\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{band\+\_\+mid,  }\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{band\+\_\+high,  }\item[{float}]{ratio1,  }\item[{float}]{ratio2,  }\item[{float}]{overlap,  }\item[{float}]{vmin,  }\item[{float}]{vmax }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Splits the input array into three bands (low, mid, and high) based on given ratios and overlap. 

This function processes the input array and divides it into three value bands\+: low, mid, and high. The bands are determined by the provided ratios and overlap. Optionally, a range (vmin, vmax) can be applied to the values in the array.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The input array that contains the data to be split into bands. \\
\hline
{\em band\+\_\+low} & The output array for the low-\/value band. \\
\hline
{\em band\+\_\+mid} & The output array for the mid-\/value band. \\
\hline
{\em band\+\_\+high} & The output array for the high-\/value band. \\
\hline
{\em ratio1} & The ratio that defines the split between the low and mid bands. \\
\hline
{\em ratio2} & The ratio that defines the split between the mid and high bands. \\
\hline
{\em overlap} & The amount of overlap between adjacent bands. \\
\hline
{\em vmin} & The minimum value for range filtering. Values below vmin will be clamped. (Optional, only in the first function) \\
\hline
{\em vmax} & The maximum value for range filtering. Values above vmax will be clamped. (Optional, only in the first function)\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

This function calculates the shaded relief map of the input array based on the sun\textquotesingle{}s azimuth (direction) and zenith (elevation) angles. The shading effect simulates the appearance of topographic features based on light direction.

Divide the path by adding points based on the lowest elevation difference between each pair of edge endpoints. 

This method uses the elevation map to subdivide the path by adding intermediate points where the elevation difference between edges is minimal. The {\ttfamily elevation\+\_\+ratio} parameter balances the influence of absolute elevation versus elevation difference in the cost function used for path finding. The {\ttfamily distance\+\_\+exponent} affects the weight function used in Dijkstra\textquotesingle{}s algorithm. Areas defined by the {\ttfamily p\+\_\+mask\+\_\+nogo} mask are avoided.

Find a Dijkstra-\/based cut path between two domain boundaries. 

Selects the lowest point on the {\ttfamily start} and {\ttfamily end} boundaries of heightmap {\ttfamily z}, then computes a path between them using a weighted Dijkstra search. The path cost combines elevation, distance, and uphill penalization. The result is returned as normalized (x, y) coordinates and elevation samples.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & Heightmap array. \\
\hline
{\em start} & Boundary where the path begins. \\
\hline
{\em end} & Boundary where the path ends. \\
\hline
{\em dijk\+\_\+elevation\+\_\+ratio} & Weight of elevation in the cost. \\
\hline
{\em dijk\+\_\+distance\+\_\+exponent} & Exponent applied to distance cost. \\
\hline
{\em dijk\+\_\+upward\+\_\+penalization} & Extra penalty for uphill moves.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Path}{Path} containing normalized (x, y) points and elevations.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Generate a stochastic cut path using midpoint displacement. 

Creates a path between the {\ttfamily start} and {\ttfamily end} boundaries of heightmap {\ttfamily z} by recursively subdividing and perturbing a segment. The result is a natural, irregular path defined by normalized (x, y) coordinates and elevations.

{\em start} & Start boundary. \\
\hline
{\em end} & End boundary. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed. \\
\hline
{\em midp\+\_\+iterations} & Number of subdivision steps. \\
\hline
{\em midp\+\_\+sigma} & Displacement amplitude.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Path}{Path} with normalized coordinates and elevations.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Finds the path with the lowest elevation and elevation difference between two points in a 2D array using Dijkstra\textquotesingle{}s algorithm. 

This function calculates the shortest path considering both elevation and elevation differences. It uses a cost function that balances between absolute elevation and elevation change. The path is determined by minimizing the combined cost function.

\begin{DoxySeeAlso}{See also}
{\bfseries [Dijkstra1971]} and \href{https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3088292}{\texttt{ https\+://math.\+stackexchange.\+com/questions/3088292}}
\end{DoxySeeAlso}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}
The {\ttfamily elevation\+\_\+ratio} parameter must be less than 1 for the algorithm to converge properly.
\end{DoxyWarning}

\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em ij\+\_\+start} & Starting coordinates (i, j) for the pathfinding. \\
\hline
{\em ij\+\_\+end} & Ending coordinates (i, j) for the pathfinding. \\
\hline
{\em i\+\_\+path\mbox{[}out\mbox{]}} & Vector to store the resulting shortest path indices in the i direction. \\
\hline
{\em j\+\_\+path\mbox{[}out\mbox{]}} & Vector to store the resulting shortest path indices in the j direction. \\
\hline
{\em elevation\+\_\+ratio} & Balance factor between absolute elevation and elevation difference in the cost function. Should be in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{[}. \\
\hline
{\em distance\+\_\+exponent} & Exponent used in the distance calculation between points. A higher exponent increases the cost of elevation gaps, encouraging the path to minimize elevation changes and reduce overall cumulative elevation gain. \\
\hline
{\em upward\+\_\+penalization} & Penalize upstream slopes. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+mask\+\_\+nogo} & Optional pointer to an array mask that defines areas to avoid during pathfinding.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Compute a path between two points using iterative midpoint refinement. 

The algorithm subdivides segments and shifts midpoints along the perpendicular direction to locally minimize the scalar field {\ttfamily z}. This is a fast heuristic alternative to graph-\/based methods (not guaranteed optimal).


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em z} & 2D scalar field (weights). \\
\hline
{\em ij\+\_\+start} & Start index. \\
\hline
{\em ij\+\_\+end} & End index. \\
\hline
{\em offset\+\_\+ratio} & Relative transverse displacement (per segment length). \\
\hline

Applies a normalization transform to the input array depending on the selected method. The operation modifies the array directly.

\item NM\+\_\+\+STANDARDIZE\+: applies z-\/score normalization (zero mean, unit variance)
\item NM\+\_\+\+ROBUST\+: applies robust scaling using median and interquartile range (IQR)

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{quilting()}{quilting()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::quilting (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const std\+::vector$<$ const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} $>$ \&}]{p\+\_\+arrays,  }\item[{glm\+::ivec2}]{patch\+\_\+base\+\_\+shape,  }\item[{glm\+::ivec2}]{tiling,  }\item[{float}]{overlap,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{std\+::vector$<$ \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} $>$}]{secondary\+\_\+arrays = {\ttfamily \{\}},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+flip = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+rotate = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+transpose = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{float}]{filter\+\_\+width\+\_\+ratio = {\ttfamily 0.25\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Synthesize a new heightmap by stitching together small patches from input heightmaps. 

This function creates a new heightmap by stitching patches from a set of input heightmaps. The stitching process allows for flipping, rotating, and transposing patches, and includes options for smoothing based on the overlap between patches. This technique is based on {\bfseries [Efros2001]}.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em p\+\_\+arrays} & Vector of pointers to input heightmaps. \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+base\+\_\+shape} & Shape of the patches to be used. \\
\hline
{\em tiling} & Number of patches in each direction (x, y). \\
\hline
{\em overlap} & Overlap between patches, in the range \mbox{]}0, 1\mbox{[}. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed number for patch placement. \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+flip} & Allow flipping of patches (up-\/down, left-\/right). \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+rotate} & Allow 90-\/degree rotation of patches (for square patches). \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+transpose} & Allow transposition of patches (for square patches). \\
\hline
{\em filter\+\_\+width\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of filter width to overlap length for smoothing. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Resulting synthesized heightmap.
\end{DoxyReturn}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::quilting\+\_\+blend (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const std\+::vector$<$ const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} $>$ \&}]{p\+\_\+arrays,  }\item[{glm\+::ivec2}]{patch\+\_\+base\+\_\+shape,  }\item[{float}]{overlap,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+flip = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+rotate = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+transpose = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{float}]{filter\+\_\+width\+\_\+ratio = {\ttfamily 0.25\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Synthesize a new heightmap by stitching together small patches from a list of input heightmaps. 

This function creates a new heightmap by stitching patches from a set of input heightmaps, similar to {\ttfamily quilting}, but the patches are blended together. The blending options include flipping, rotating, and transposing patches, with smoothing based on the overlap between patches.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em p\+\_\+arrays} & Vector of pointers to input heightmaps. \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+base\+\_\+shape} & Shape of the patches to be used. \\
\hline
{\em overlap} & Overlap between patches, in the range \mbox{]}0, 1\mbox{[}. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed number for patch placement. \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+flip} & Allow flipping of patches (up-\/down, left-\/right). \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+rotate} & Allow 90-\/degree rotation of patches (for square patches). \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+transpose} & Allow transposition of patches (for square patches). \\
\hline
{\em filter\+\_\+width\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of filter width to overlap length for smoothing. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Resulting synthesized heightmap.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{quilting\_expand()}{quilting\_expand()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::quilting\+\_\+expand (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{float}]{expansion\+\_\+ratio,  }\item[{glm\+::ivec2}]{patch\+\_\+base\+\_\+shape,  }\item[{float}]{overlap,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{std\+::vector$<$ \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} $>$}]{secondary\+\_\+arrays = {\ttfamily \{\}},  }\item[{bool}]{keep\+\_\+input\+\_\+shape = {\ttfamily false},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+flip = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+rotate = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+transpose = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{float}]{filter\+\_\+width\+\_\+ratio = {\ttfamily 0.25\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Synthesize a new heightmap by expanding the input heightmap and stitching patches. 

This function generates a larger heightmap by expanding the input heightmap and stitching patches based on the given parameters. The expansion ratio determines the new size of the heightmap, and the function includes options for flipping, rotating, and transposing patches. The output can be either the same shape as the input or expanded based on the given ratio.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input heightmap to be expanded. \\
\hline
{\em expansion\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio by which to expand the heightmap (e.\+g., 2 for doubling the size). \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+base\+\_\+shape} & Shape of the patches to be used. \\
\hline
{\em overlap} & Overlap between patches, in the range \mbox{]}0, 1\mbox{[}. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed number for patch placement. \\
\hline
{\em keep\+\_\+input\+\_\+shape} & If true, the output heightmap retains the input shape. \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+flip} & Allow flipping of patches (up-\/down, left-\/right). \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+rotate} & Allow 90-\/degree rotation of patches (for square patches). \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+transpose} & Allow transposition of patches (for square patches). \\
\hline
{\em filter\+\_\+width\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of filter width to overlap length for smoothing. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Resulting synthesized heightmap.
\end{DoxyReturn}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{quilting\_shuffle()}{quilting\_shuffle()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} hmap\+::quilting\+\_\+shuffle (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \&}]{array,  }\item[{glm\+::ivec2}]{patch\+\_\+base\+\_\+shape,  }\item[{float}]{overlap,  }\item[{std\+::uint32\+\_\+t}]{seed,  }\item[{std\+::vector$<$ \mbox{\hyperlink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} $>$}]{secondary\+\_\+arrays = {\ttfamily \{\}},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+flip = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+rotate = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{bool}]{patch\+\_\+transpose = {\ttfamily true},  }\item[{float}]{filter\+\_\+width\+\_\+ratio = {\ttfamily 0.25\mbox{\hyperlink{distance__transform_8cpp_abcb9259cf91bfd25e92a72cdf18c285e}{f}}} }\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Synthesize a new heightmap by reshuffling patches of the input heightmap. 

This function generates a new heightmap by reshuffling patches of the input heightmap, effectively creating a new pattern while keeping the same shape as the input heightmap. The function includes options for patch flipping, rotating, and transposing.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & Input heightmap to be reshuffled. \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+base\+\_\+shape} & Shape of the patches to be used. \\
\hline
{\em overlap} & Overlap between patches, in the range \mbox{]}0, 1\mbox{[}. \\
\hline
{\em seed} & Random seed number for patch placement. \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+flip} & Allow flipping of patches (up-\/down, left-\/right). \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+rotate} & Allow 90-\/degree rotation of patches (for square patches). \\
\hline
{\em patch\+\_\+transpose} & Allow transposition of patches (for square patches). \\
\hline
{\em filter\+\_\+width\+\_\+ratio} & Ratio of filter width to overlap length for smoothing. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
\doxylink{classhmap_1_1Array}{Array} Resulting synthesized heightmap with reshuffled patches.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Applies a zoom effect to a 2D array with an adjustable center. 

This function scales the input 2D array by a specified zoom factor, effectively resizing the array\textquotesingle{}s contents. The zoom operation is centered around a specified point within the array, allowing for flexible zooming behavior. The function supports both periodic boundary conditions, where the array wraps around, and non-\/periodic conditions, where areas outside the original array bounds are filled with zeros.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em array} & The input 2D array to be zoomed. This array remains unmodified. \\
\hline
{\em zoom\+\_\+factor} & The factor by which to zoom the array. A value greater than 1 enlarges the contents, while a value between 0 and 1 reduces them. \\
\hline
{\em periodic} & If set to {\ttfamily true}, the zoom is periodic, meaning that elements moving out of the array bounds due to the zoom reappear on the opposite side. If {\ttfamily false}, areas outside the original array bounds are filled with zeros. The default is {\ttfamily false}. \\
\hline
{\em center} & The center of the zoom operation, specified as a {\ttfamily glm\+::vec2} with coordinates in the range \mbox{[}0, 1\mbox{]}, where \{0.\+5f, 0.\+5f\} represents the center of the array. The default center is \{0.\+5f, 0.\+5f\}. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+x} & Optional pointer to a 2D array that contains x-\/direction noise to be added during the zoom operation. If provided, the noise values are applied to the x-\/coordinates of the zoomed array on a per-\/element basis. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise\+\_\+y} & Optional pointer to a 2D array that contains y-\/direction noise to be added during the zoom operation. If provided, the noise values are applied to the y-\/coordinates of the zoomed array on a per-\/element basis. \\
\hline
{\em bbox} & Domain bounding box.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
A new 2D array that is the result of applying the zoom effect to the input {\ttfamily array} by the specified {\ttfamily zoom\+\_\+factor} and centered at the specified {\ttfamily center}.
\end{DoxyReturn}

Colorize two scalar fields into a \doxylink{classhmap_1_1VirtualTexture}{Virtual\+Texture} using two custom colormaps and a color mixing method. 


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em out} & Output virtual texture. \\
\hline
{\em a1} & First input scalar field. \\
\hline
{\em a2} & Second input scalar field. \\
\hline
{\em cm} & Compute mode (CPU/\+GPU). \\
\hline
{\em range1} & Lower and upper bounds for normalization of the first field. \\
\hline
{\em range2} & Lower and upper bounds for normalization of the second field. \\
\hline
{\em positions1} & Normalized color positions for the first colormap. \\
\hline
{\em positions2} & Normalized color positions for the second colormap. \\
\hline
{\em colormap\+\_\+colors1} & RGB colors for the first colormap. \\
\hline
{\em colormap\+\_\+colors2} & RGB colors for the second colormap. \\
\hline
{\em method} & Method used to mix the two resulting colors. \\
\hline
{\em reverse1} & Reverse the first colormap mapping. \\
\hline
{\em reverse2} & Reverse the second colormap mapping. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise1} & Optional noise added to the first scalar field before normalization. \\
\hline
{\em p\+\_\+noise2} & Optional noise added to the second scalar field before normalization. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Compute luminance from a \doxylink{classhmap_1_1VirtualTexture}{Virtual\+Texture}. 

Computes a grayscale luminance array from the RGB channels of a virtual texture and stores the result in {\ttfamily out}.


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em out} & Output luminance array. \\
\hline
{\em tex} & Input virtual texture (expects at least 3 channels). \\
\hline
{\em cm} & Compute mode (execution and storage behavior). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
